Despite his recent captures, Olin Umberhide seems to be a tauren of some skill in combat. He certainly has learned how to get an enemy's attention.

I have a mission available that might prove ideal for his skill sets.

When you are ready, simply issue the order via the command table in front of me and we will dispatch him immediately.

passages.title: Mission Probable
passages.text: Commander, I have a mission that might suite your new follower quite well.

passages.title: Mission Probable
passages.text: As additional missions come to my attention I will make them available here.

passages.title: Gatekeepers of Auchindoun
passages.text:
I was taken captive by the Iron Horde when they raided our caravan en route to Auchindoun.

I escaped, but these spirits won't let me through to join my fellow Sunsworn until someone defeats them in combat!

Please, will you help me defeat them?

passages.title: Gatekeepers of Auchindoun
passages.text: I appreciate all of your help, hero.

passages.title: Gatekeepers of Auchindoun
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>. I am truly in your debt.

When I fulfill my duties to Lady Liadrin I will come find you.

passages.title: Gatekeepers of Auchindoun
passages.text:
Auchindoun is under attack, stranger, and I intend to help defend it.

The only problem is the only armor I could find was my grandfather's old set, and it isn't nearly enough to defeat the spirits blocking the path toward Auchindoun.

Would you defeat them and let me through the gate with you? I will find a way to repay you!

passages.title: Gatekeepers of Auchindoun
passages.text: I will defend Auchindoun with my life. We cannot lose anymore in this war!

passages.title: Gatekeepers of Auchindoun
passages.text: You have my eternal gratitude, hero. I will find a way to repay you someday.

passages.title: Defenstrations
passages.text:
No sooner does power rush to the crystal outside than you hear distant war cries and shouts of alarm. Elodor is being attacked!

If you want your laborers to come home in one piece, you'd best help with the defense of the town. Defeat the invasion and then return to the control console to reset the defenses.

passages.title: Defenstrations
passages.text: The sounds of attack still reverberate from outside, which is alarming, given that the console seems awash with angrily blinking warning indicators.

passages.title: Defenstrations
passages.text:
You saved the town! The controls shut down as you approach, but many of the indicators are still blinking frantically. Something seems wrong.

Hataaru yells out to get your attention outside...

passages.title: The Exarch Council
passages.text:
Good work at the gates! The Shadowmoon orcs have been seeking prisoners for some reason. Their aggression helps our cause.

Come with me. I would like to introduce you to the Exarch Council, "The Hand of the Prophet." I have been trying to convince the Exarchs to support our cause and go on the offensive against the Iron Horde, but they are - as always - too cautious and slow to act.

Come with me, I will introduce you to Exarch Othaar up the hill. Perhaps meeting an Alliance hero can sway the council.

passages.title: The Exarch Council
passages.text:
<Exarch Othaar is a towering, intimidating figure. His eyes bore into you, determining if you are friend or foe.>

So, you are <name>, esteemed <class> of this "Alliance" that has appeared on our shores. On behalf of the Exarch Council, I welcome you to Elodor.

passages.title: Naielle, The Rangari
passages.text:
I am calling the Exarch Council to order to hear your petition. None of us doubt that this "Iron Horde" is a threat, but few can agree on what we should do about it. It is up to you and Vindicator Maraad to gather the Exarchs together.

Exarch Naielle is the leader of the Rangari, the "Eyes of the Prophet." They are our scouts who silently stalk the farthest corners of Draenor. Seek her out in the Rangari Enclave northwest of here.

passages.title: Naielle, The Rangari
passages.text:
<name>! You have only just arrived but already your name is the talk of Elodor.

I will gladly support your cause for the Exarch Council - it has always been my opinion that the draenei need to get out and be proactive in our world instead of hiding behind our walls.

But first, I need your help with something...

passages.title: Hataaru, the Artificer
passages.text:
I will also need you to call upon Exarch Hataaru. I understand you were helping him with our defenses at the gate.

Hataaru is our Chief Artificer - he understands our technology better than any other and has been working tirelessly to recreate the glory of the civilization we left behind.

He has moved to his workstation outside of the Elodor Dig, our crystal mines located just to the Southeast. Look for him at the mine entrance.

passages.title: Hataaru, the Artificer
passages.text:
Ah, <name>! I suspected I would see you again soon.

I am willing to speak on your behalf at the Exarch Council, but an emergency situation has come up...

passages.title: Taking the Fight to Nagrand
passages.text:
Boss-mon, good to see ya.

Durotan recommended dat we be gettin' a foothold in Nagrand, so I taken the liberty of dispatchin' some of da boys.

Thrall's already reportin' that the outside be nearly complete. He been askin' me to let ya know they be ready for ya.

A windrider be waitin' to catch ya up with the latest caravan shipment whenever you be ready, <sir/ma'am>.

passages.title: Taking the Fight to Nagrand
passages.text:
They came at us... from... nowhere.

<The stoneguard nearly passes out.>

passages.title: The Might of the Warsong
passages.text:
<The officer is in a great deal of pain. It's clear that he's not long for this world.>

The Warsong. Surprise attack.

Headed into... the Burning Blade....

<He takes a moment, before continuing.>

They took the... blueprints....

<These are his last words.>

passages.title: The Might of the Warsong
passages.text:
Commander <name>. It's good to see you. We have much to discuss.

The situation in Nagrand is rapidly deteriorating. The Warsong clan is on the move.

To make matters worse, Grommash has named Garrosh their new warlord.

passages.title: A Pilgrimage Gone Awry
passages.text:
I am a humble pilgrim, I swear. Please don't hurt me!

My sister and I were traveling to Auchindoun to pay our respects to my grandmother when we hit an overturned rock and lost control of our caravan. I managed to survive, but my sister...

<Nadur cries.>

Please, you have to help me. I'm desperate. If you could bring me some prowler blood, snapdragon flowers, and a riverhopper eye, I can fashion a potion to bring her back. I just know it....

passages.title: A Pilgrimage Gone Awry
passages.text: Tuliaa isn't just my sister. She's my best friend.

passages.title: A Pilgrimage Gone Awry
passages.text: Thank you, stranger.

passages.title: A Pilgrimage Gone Awry
passages.text:
My sister and I were traveling to Auchindoun to pay our respects to my grandmother when we hit an overturned rock and lost control of our caravan. I managed to survive, but my sister...

<Nadur cries.>

Please, I need your help. If you could bring me some prowler blood, snapdragon flowers, and a riverhopper eye, I can fashion a potion to bring her back... I just know I can...

passages.title: A Pilgrimage Gone Awry
passages.text: I don't know what I would do without Tuliaa... she's not just my sister. She's my best friend.

passages.title: A Pilgrimage Gone Awry
passages.text: Thank you, a thousand times thank you.

passages.title: Echo Hunters
passages.text:
I am no sorcerer, but I've picked up a few spells in my time - enough for me to pass unseen by the naked eye.

Unfortunately, the vampire bats in these woods don't use their eyes. They will hear my shuffling robes and Percy's incessant clucking a mile away.

Clear them away from the path, would you?

passages.title: Echo Hunters
passages.text: Blasted things. Nothing more than flying rats if you ask me!

passages.title: Prune the Podlings
passages.text:
The blood soaked body of Ryan is slumped up against the cave wall. Tiny teeth marks cover his body.

The podlings clearly are a threat to you and your garrison.

It's time to do a little pruning.

passages.title: More Lazy Peons
passages.text:
We have a rare opportunity to strike at the heart of the Warsong. But, we need your wisdom and leadership.

The most important decision will be your choice between building a corral or a tankworks. This choice will setup our approach to the fight against the Warsong.

Thazz'ril will head up our building efforts. Will you give him a hand?

It looks like he's having trouble motivating his peons to work.

passages.title: More Lazy Peons
passages.text: If there's one thing the Horde never seems to be short on, it's lazy peons.

passages.title: More Lazy Peons
passages.text: I knew it was a mistake to bring these guys with me from the Valley of Trials.

passages.title: A Lesson in Mineralogy
passages.text:
<Gazmolf gestures at the large machine nearby.>

I built this machine to break down elementium minerals into base elements. You see, it's not just what's buried within the ground that can be valuable; but also the ground itself!

Take, for example, the earth elementals below us; inside every earth elemental is an earthen core, dense in precious metal!.

Those elementals are going to make us rich! Collect several earthen cores, place them in the Gold-O-Matic 9000, and I'll give you a cut!

passages.title: A Lesson in Mineralogy
passages.text: <The Gold-O-Matic 9000 buzzes and whirrs with the sounds of heavy machinery.>

passages.title: A Lesson in Mineralogy
passages.text:
<The Gold-O-Matic 9000 crunches and grinds through the elemental remains.>

chakk-chackk-chak-chak, chak-a-chak-akk-chk-chk-chk.

passages.title: Gazmolf Futzwangler and the Highmaul Crusade
passages.text:
I'm here in Nagrand recruiting for the Steamwheedle Preservation Society. We're the archaeological branch of the Steamwheedle Cartel.

We're here to collect all of the artifacts, relics, antiquities and oddities that Nagrand has to offer! Currently, we're hiring surveyors, excavators, adventurers... you name it!

If you're interested in getting your hands dirty, talk to Gazmolf Futzwangler over at Stonecrag Gorge. He's the goblin in charge of this expedition!

passages.title: Gazmolf Futzwangler and the Highmaul Crusade
passages.text:
It's good to see that there's still an interest out there in real archaeology!

There's a lot of misconceptions out there about how archaeology is really done, but have no fear! The great and famous Gazmolf Futzwangler is here to educate you.

passages.title: Good Help is Hard to Find
passages.text:
The excavation team is on strike!

Foreman Thazwix and his cronies think they can squeeze the Steamwheedle Preservation Society for some extra dough by refusing to work.

What I need is a scab, a strikebreaker; someone to put some pressure on them by doing the job they refuse to do!

Go down into the gorge, dig up some antiquities for me, and I'll pay you what I would have payed those lazy numbskulls!

passages.title: Good Help is Hard to Find
passages.text: Do you have the Nagrand Antiquities?

passages.title: Good Help is Hard to Find
passages.text:
Great work, <name>!

That bunch of good-for-nothing's came crying when they found out someone else was making their money! I don't think Thazwix, or his cronies, will be much trouble from here on out.

As promised, here's the pay I owe you for a job well done!

passages.title: Making Acquaintances
passages.text:
It's nice to see someone else taking a vested interest in the arcane arts, you know. It's all too rare these days if you ask me!

Unfortunately, I must meet Cordana to handle an important matter, but we're in luck! One of my good friends in the Kirin Tor has agreed to help you connect your arcane sanctum to the ley line network.

He's waiting at my tower. Let's leave immediately and introduce you to one another.

passages.title: Making Acquaintances
passages.text: You are <name>, I presume?

passages.title: Making Acquaintances
passages.text:
I am Magister Krelas. Pyromaniac.

Pleasure.

passages.title: Making Acquaintances
passages.text:
It's nice to see someone else taking a vested interest in the arcane arts, you know. It's all too rare these days if you ask me.

Unfortunately, I must meet Cordana to handle an important matter, but we're in luck! One of my good friends in the Kirin Tor has agreed to help you connect your arcane sanctum to the ley line network.

She's waiting at my tower. Let's leave immediately and introduce you to one another.

passages.title: Making Acquaintances
passages.text:
Nice to meet you.

I am Magister Serena. Frost mage extraordinaire!

passages.title: Altar Altercation
They Call Him Lantresor of the Blade
passages.text:
The garrison blueprints were taken to the Burning Blade village when the Warsong sacked your caravan. I can't construct this building without those plans.

There's been talk of a young blademaster who's been exiled from the clan for many years. They call him Lantresor of the Blade.

Our scouts recently saw him return to Hallvalor to challenge the blademaster leadership. Instead, they clapped him in chains.

Maybe he's still alive. Maybe he'll help you recover the blueprints?

passages.title: They Call Him Lantresor of the Blade
passages.text:
Who are you?

Don't you know death by sight, <class>?

passages.title: Fruitful Ventures
passages.text:
Oh no! They must be vegetarians.

What these elekk need is fruit and lots of it. There are cherries all over the place around here under the trees.

You wouldn't mind grabbing me some, would ya?

passages.title: Fruitful Ventures
passages.text:
I heard the worst rumor about how you have to obtain those things.

Something about talbuk first eating them and then 'processing' them, and then... well, I don't want to talk about it.

passages.title: Fruitful Ventures
passages.text: You got them all? I just know this is going to work.

passages.title: Lost Lumberjacks
passages.text:
Shelly and her crew haven't returned from Gloomshade Grove.

It's been days... I hope everything is okay.

passages.title: Lost Lumberjacks
passages.text: This is one of the pack mules Shelly and her crew took to Gloomshade Grove.

passages.title: What We Need
passages.text:
I heard you guys hijacked and wrecked a ship on your way out of Tanaan.

It's like my daddy always said: One man's wreck is another goblin's workshop.

You should head down to the coast west of the garrison and see if you can't find any materials we might salvage. Oh, and uh... should probably watch yourself. I hear there are ogre raiders in the area.

passages.title: What We Need
passages.text: How's the salvage operation comin'?

passages.title: What We Need
passages.text: Hey... now that is some nice salvage. Say what you will about the Iron Horde, but they got some serious raw materials to work with.

passages.title: The Ogron Live?
passages.text:
Commander, our Frostwolf allies reportin' dat the Bladespire ogres have an outpost to our west led by an ogron.

I heard tales of da ogron but never seen one. Dey be brutes, creatures from a time that was best left forgotten. Dey say most were slain during the forming of the original horde. What dey lack in wisdom they make up for in violence, force, and greed.

I counsel dispatchin' dis creature as soon as possible.

passages.title: The Ogron Live?
passages.text: Where the ogron goes, death and pain are sure to follow.

passages.title: The Ogron Live?
passages.text: Well done, boss-mon. The Bladespire ogres been pullin' back their raiding parties. But ya can bet dey be comin' back, and in larger numbers. The threat from their citadel must be dealt with soon.

passages.title: The Friend of My Enemy
passages.text:
Hallvalor is the ancestral home of the Burning Blade clan. Since they're such fast friends, the Warsong have allowed the blademasters to remain in Nagrand.

We are fierce, but we won't win if the Burning Blade attack us. It would be wise to strike first.

passages.title: The Friend of My Enemy
passages.text:
A great victory over the Burning Blade!

This new Warlord Azuka Bladefury sounds formidable. We will have to keep an eye on her and her blademasters.

passages.title: Ishaal's Orb
passages.text:
The Adherents came for me, but I was already hiding. I watched from the shadows as they ransacked my hut.

Then I watched the Shattered Hand orcs arrive and butcher them like dinner fowl. Seems everyone is after us these days.

One of those orc thugs made off with my scrying orb. I will be needing it back if I am to be of any use to Iskar.

passages.title: Ishaal's Orb
passages.text: Have you found the orb?

passages.title: Ishaal's Orb
passages.text:
Hmm... something's not right. She's been tampered with.

Someone else has used my orb to enter the realm of shadows.

passages.title: New Neighbors
passages.text:
The Shattered Hand clan is made up of orcs who can call no other clan home. They are sadistic warriors who maim their bodies, perhaps in a show of solidarity or perhaps because they simply enjoy the pain.

It does not matter. What matters is that they are expanding their territory, butchering anyone in their path.

They must be dealt with.

passages.title: New Neighbors
passages.text: Blood for blood, as it should be.

passages.title: Lunarblossom
passages.text:
How I long to hold Kat'la.

No star or moon can compare to her beauty.

Alas, I am but a simple boar farmer.

If only I could find time to sneak away from this pathetic excuse for a job and pick some lunarblossoms for Kat'la.

I wouldn't dare confess my love to her without a gift.

passages.title: Lunarblossom
passages.text: How can I help you, <class>?

passages.title: Lunarblossom
passages.text: Lunarblossoms! You are too kind! I can't wait to give these to Kat'la.

passages.title: Going to the Gordunni
passages.text:
We have a good supply of jovite in the arsenal now but there just isn't enough of the material in the mine to keep us in stock for long. Down south of here there's a mountain that's just full of the stuff but there's one problem; Ogres!

The Gordunni live on top of that mountain and they have begun trading the jovite to the Iron Horde.

We need to go down there and secure the minerals for ourselves.

I'll pack some supplies and meet you near their fortress down south.

passages.title: Going to the Gordunni
passages.text:
I crafted a few things before we left that we may need: some bombs, a grappling hook, even was able to get one of the goblins to get a spare rocket pack.

I'm sure we'll find a use for everything.

passages.title: Ikky's Egg
passages.text:
<Miraculously, this single egg has eluded the ravagers.

A small tag has been lovingly tied around the base of the egg. It reads "Ikky.">

passages.title: Ikky's Egg
passages.text: <The hatchling springs immediately to flight, then looks at you expectantly and cheeps.>

passages.title: Dropping Bombs
passages.text:
The Gordunni have only a single path to their fortress and it is well-defended from a large attack.

Thankfully they wont be expecting just the two of us to be attempting to break in.

This is a great opportunity to take out their defenses and get some target practice for our artillery gunners back at the arsenal.

Take these smoke grenades and use it to call in an artillery strike on their catapults as we head up.

passages.title: Dropping Bombs
passages.text: Now that we're inside we have much to do.

passages.title: The Den of Skog
passages.text: Olin Umberhide appears to have discovered the parent of the gronnlings and is outmatched by himself. He will be slain without help.

passages.title: We Require More Resources
passages.text:
So what we got here is a good start, but you are looking for something that can support ARMIES!

Truth is, we ain't building anything without the materials to build it, and our supplies from Azeroth are limited.

I got some ideas on how to get you started but you are going to have to keep your eyes open for more materials when out in the field. Lots of useful stuff out there we can change into usable material.

passages.title: Lurking in the Shadows
passages.text:
There are reports of Shadowmoon clan members lurking around the ruins by the shore.

This is a popular spot for young lovers to gaze at the stars and confess their affection for each other.

As you can see we are not a village of warriors.

I will pay you handsomely if you go to the ruins and make sure the Shadowmoon orcs keep their distance.

passages.title: Fish Fight
passages.text: We have an accessible fishing spot here, but no bait seems to work! We need to find a local fisherman with some knowledge of the area to help us out. Think you are up to the task?

passages.title: The Blade Itself
passages.text:
When they clapped me in irons, the Burning Blade instructor, Luhk the Keen-Eyed, took my blade. He's an honorable orc, even if his training techniques are counter-productive.

I want my blade back, <class>. Then, I'll break myself free.

passages.title: The Blade Itself
passages.text: A blademaster without a blade is no blademaster at all.

passages.title: The Blade Itself
passages.text: If you can defeat Luhk, then perhaps there's some hope for you after all.

passages.title: Vignette: Gruuk
passages.text:
Goren are dangerous, especially in large numbers, and especially when we have a blind, under powered shaman with us.

Fortunately, they have very short lifespans. Unfortunately, they multiply fast and grow faster.

If we are going to do this we need to find the brood mother. Slaying her and her eggs should slow down the onslaught of goren. Check the burrows near the Forge Gates and I will to keep them off of Drek'Thar's scent.

passages.title: Punching Through
passages.text:
To secure the fortress we need to kill Witch Lord Morkurk, but I don't think we should go straight after him.

His three lieutenants - Vorgorsh, Zulmork, and Cromaug - are all powerful mages, and all of them are fiercely loyal to Morkurk.

I suspect that if we engage the Witch Lord that they will rush to his aid. Let's take them out so that cannot happen.

passages.title: Punching Through
passages.text: We need to make sure those Vizier's are taken care of before we can deal with Morkurk.

passages.title: Punching Through
passages.text:
Now with the viziers gone the whole Gordunni enchantment trade with the Iron Horde will come crashing down!

We can now turn our attention to dealing with Morkurk.

passages.title: Supply Recovery
passages.text:
We seem to have arrived at just the right time!

The Gordunni have been enchanting armaments for the Iron Horde and it looks like they haven't picked up the latest shipment.

We could put that gear to far better use! Lets go hunt down their shipping containers. I brought some signal flares that we can use to call in an air pick-up when we've secured the shipment.

passages.title: Supply Recovery
passages.text: The goblins said that the flares would surely get their attention. I just hope it doesn't come from the hillside being blown apart.

passages.title: Supply Recovery
passages.text:
Alright, that should be the last one we need. 

Nothing feels as good as knowing you are stronger than your enemy!

passages.title: We Need An Army
passages.text:
So the new warchief decided to send you Warmaster Zog to handle local operations. Zog!

I heard that guy was notorious for organizing the Alliance AND the Horde to face off against the silithid at the Gates of Ahn'Qiraj.

He was a general back then.

Anyway, if you go let him know about the barracks being done I'm sure he'll have some thoughts on how to put it to good use.

You can find Zog up at the town hall.

passages.title: We Need An Army
passages.text: Commander, it is an honor to serve you.

passages.title: Meet Me in the Cavern
passages.text:
It's time, <class>. Time for you to get your blueprints.

Time for us to face the masters.

passages.title: Meet Me in the Cavern
passages.text:
You made it. Good.

Getting in here was nothing compared to what's to come.

passages.title: The Secrets of Gorgrond
passages.text:
Commander, I will leave my forces to secure this pass, but I will not sit idle while our enemy prepares for another attack.

I want to take the fight to the heart of the Iron Horde at Blackrock, and to do that we are going to need to go where few orcs dare tread.

Gorgrond.

It is a savage place, filled with giants and monsters of every sort.

Will you dare these wilds with me so that we might strike at the foundries of the Iron Horde?

passages.title: The Secrets of Gorgrond
passages.text: Gorgrond is no place for armies, commander. We are now stepping into the domain of legends.

passages.title: Tastes Like Chicken
passages.text:
You got a moment, <bub/beautiful>? I've got an elekk-sized problem.

Someone, um, sold me... yeah, sold me these two, but they're sick. I've tried everything, but nothing I do makes any difference!

I think they must be starving. I heard that elekk like raw windroc. Gross if you ask me.

Anyway, while you're out doing your thing, you mind picking me up some bird meat?

passages.title: Tastes Like Chicken
passages.text:
Windrocs? Yeah, Nagrand's filthy with them.

They seem to like high places and rock outcroppings.

I don't know. What do I look like - a windroc whisperer? You're the <class>.

passages.title: Tastes Like Chicken
passages.text:
It sure doesn't smell like chicken!

Okay, okay, hand it over. I'll feed them and then everyone will be happy and I can turn a tidy - er, um... they'll feel better.

Yeah.

passages.title: Next Steps
passages.text:
You are positively on fire!

We have everything I need to create the scroll. Your arcane sanctum will be brimming with arcane energy in no time.

I will teleport to Vol'jin's Pride to combine the reagents and marshal your forces. Meet me there when you can.

passages.title: Next Steps
passages.text:
Your forces burn with passion for your cause.

Not easy against such towering foes. Well done.

passages.title: Next Steps
passages.text:
We did it! We have all of the reagents for the scroll. Your arcane sanctum will be the talk of Draenor before long.

I'll go back to Fort Wrynn to finish it and gather your men. Meet me there.

passages.title: Next Steps
passages.text: Now we can tackle getting that artificial nexus for your tower.

passages.title: Removing the Reinforcements
passages.text:
My own investigations have uncovered a permanent arcane portal from here to Highmaul itself.

It is guarded but shouldn't be too hard to disrupt once you've gotten some breathing room.

passages.title: Removing the Reinforcements
passages.text:
Excellent.  I doubt they will rebuild it after we've completed all of our objectives here.

This place will return to being a failing outpost for the Gorian Empire.

passages.title: The Foot of the Fortress
passages.text:
We've enkindled your forces and the scroll is ready.

It's time for phase two - stealing a nexus crystal from a heavily fortified ogre compound.

We'll save the scroll to bring in reinforcements in our confrontation with the Gordunni Witch Lord. Let's meet at the base of the Gordal Foothills and take what is more or less rightfully yours!

passages.title: The Foot of the Fortress
passages.text:
My apologies for teleporting away. It's cheating, I know.

I merely wanted to put a fire under your feet to get here quickly!

passages.title: Dropping In
passages.text:
Witch Lord Morkurk is no fool.

He has catapults set up throughout the foothills leading into their compound.

No matter, I have a way to handle them.

Take out the ogres guarding the siege weapons and mark them once they're clear. I'm readying a vortex spell that will handle things from there.

We'll meet just outside their gate afterwards.

passages.title: Dropping In
passages.text: Before we take on Morkurk we have some business to attend to in the fortress proper.

passages.title: Blades in the Dark
passages.text:
Those orcs got hold of Ishaal's orb, did they? That would explain the dangerous-looking fellow who crossed into this realm shortly before you.

Not everyone handles the transition as... gracefully as you did. The oaf is still grappling with his own mind, stumbling about and muttering nonsense.

Soon he will be drawn to the orb again, which would presumably lead him to Veil Terokk.

Better to take him out now while he's still befuddled.

passages.title: Blades in the Dark
passages.text: He was a big boy, wasn't he? The fiends will make quite a feast of him.

passages.title: A Feast of Shadows
passages.text:
Many arakkoa died in Veil Akraz. From the outside, all seems still. Empty.

But in this place between worlds, death never goes unnoticed.

Stray life essence seeps through from the other side; a feast for the beings who prowl here.

Slay the shadow creatures here, and gather from their corpses the fine dust they produce. I will need much of it to perform the rites of the Talon King.

passages.title: A Feast of Shadows
passages.text:
You know those elixirs you have been so eagerly quaffing?

They are made of this stuff.

passages.title: A Feast of Shadows
passages.text: Good. With this much dust we can delve deep enough to reach the Talon King's refuge.

passages.title: The Kaliri Whisperer
passages.text:
An important contact lives in the nearby Shadowglade. He is meek, but trains kaliri of monstrous size which are quite dangerous.

He once claimed they could knock a rylak out of the sky, but I'll believe that when I see it.

Skizzik is holding a valuable treasure for me. Seek him out and get him back to Veil Terokk if you can. At the very least, recover the gavel I entrusted to him.

passages.title: The Kaliri Whisperer
passages.text: Any word on Skizzik?

passages.title: The Kaliri Whisperer
passages.text:
I see. Well, at least the gavel is safe.

As you may have guessed, it is another of the Talon King's relics.

passages.title: Mother of Thorns
passages.text:
<Beneath Skizzik's outstretched hand, letters are scrawled into the dirt:

t h o r n

m o t h e r

Ravagers brought in by the Shattered Hand have taken over the aviary and are breeding fast. If left alone, they could be swarming the entire area - including Veil Terokk - in a matter of days.>

passages.title: Mother of Thorns
passages.text:
Shame about Skizzik's aviary. That's where Percy came from. Skizzik wasn't interested in the "runts" after he started breeding the big ones full-time.

To be honest, I never liked those monstrous things.

passages.title: Baby Bird
passages.text:
<Ikky cheeps again, then begins gnawing on his foot.

Looking out across the nearby hillside, you spy tiny ravager grubs inching along the grass.>

passages.title: Baby Bird
passages.text: <Ikky looks up at you, foot clamped in his beak, and lets out a muffled cheep.>

passages.title: Baby Bird
passages.text:
<You hold the handful of grubs out, steel yourself, and prepare to chew them up as a mama bird would.

Thankfully, Ikky snatches them from your hand before you can proceed.

Apparently kaliri don't do that.>

passages.title: While We're in the Neighborhood
passages.text:
Ah, the hubris of ogres.

It always backfires.

Morkurk has been using enchanted bracelets to empower his minions with arcane strength.

We can disenchant these bracelets into reagents that will no doubt be useful to your arcane sanctum. What do you think about collecting some while we're here?

passages.title: While We're in the Neighborhood
passages.text: Most mages discount the use of arcane dust these days, but they're wrong.

passages.title: While We're in the Neighborhood
passages.text: Yes, these will definitely be useful! Trust me.

passages.title: Vicious Viziers
passages.text:
We're after Witch Lord Morkurk, but we shouldn't charge straight at him.

His three lieutenants - Vorgorsh, Zulmork, and Cromaug - are the only other capable mages left of the Gordunni, and are fiercely loyal to Morkurk.

I suspect that if we engage the Witch Lord that they will rush to his aid. Let's take them out first.

passages.title: Vicious Viziers
passages.text: I don't take chances.

passages.title: Vicious Viziers
passages.text: Now that they're out of the way, Morkurk is exposed.

passages.title: Orbs of Power
passages.text:
There's a minor fire we'll need to put out before we can enact my plan.

Morkurk has placed powerful wards throughout Gordal Fortress that will prevent any sort of mass summoning - awfully detrimental to our scroll of mass teleportation.

Thankfully, no ogre would ever consider that a single enemy or two would have the gall to breach their walls.

passages.title: Orbs of Power
passages.text:
There's nothing Morkurk can do to stop us now.

Well done indeed!

passages.title: Elemental Attunement
passages.text:
Many shaman have sought the favor of the Throne of Elements.

Forming an elemental bond with the furies allows a shaman to not only know the will of the elements on Draenor, but also tap into a great font of elemental power.

If you are to discover the truth behind Gordawg's disappearance, you will need to succeed where others have failed and undertake the Ritual of Binding.

First, you must prepare yourself. Seek out the elemental pillars upon the plateau and attune your spirit with the elements.

passages.title: Elemental Attunement
passages.text:
You have done well, <name>.

By linking with each of the four elemental pillars you have attuned your life energy with each of the elements on Draenor.

You are now ready to undertake the Ritual of Binding.

Speak to me when your work upon the Elemental Plateau is finished, and we shall begin.

passages.title: Guardians of the Plateau
passages.text:
The Elemental Plateau is sanctuary to the elemental spirits of Nagrand.

The greatest among the elementals on the plateau are the guardians; mighty elemental spirits that stand watch over their domain.

The guardians are pure and mighty spirits but a disturbance in the natural balance has caused them to grow unstable, corrupting the lesser elementals around them.

In order to restore balance to the plateau, the guardians must be destroyed. Only then will the cycle of rebirth begin.

passages.title: Guardians of the Plateau
passages.text:
Each of the guardians you put to rest were once mighty and noble elemental spirits.

In time each shall be reborn anew through the cycle of rebirth, but Gordawg must be found and balance restored lest the plateau become unstable yet again.

passages.title: A Rare Bloom
passages.text:
Many years ago I had a life-mate, Dahaka. We were only bound a short time before she was taken from me.

I have lived long, but I have never known greater pain than that day. I was young and my grief was great; the earth quaked beneath my rage. I laid her to rest upon this cliff.

It is here where I too will rest, but first a favor.

A rare bloom grows in a cave within the fiery, molten earth of the plateau. It was her favorite.

I would lay the flower upon her grave one last time before I die.

passages.title: A Rare Bloom
passages.text: Do you have the Ember Blossom?

passages.title: A Rare Bloom
passages.text: This is a fine Ember Blossom that you have brought to me. I know the danger you faced to retrieve it and I thank you.

passages.title: Rangari Roundup
passages.text:
You have a keen eye, <class>.

There are Rangari like myself hidden throughout the Nightmarsh.

I need reports from each of them to ensure the area is safe.

Perhaps you can help me?

passages.title: Rangari Roundup
passages.text: Thank you for the report, <name>. We must keep a close eye on these southern wilds.

passages.title: New Babies
passages.text:
That's better, but there's still something wrong. I'm getting desperate here, <name>.

Can I call ya, <name>? Great.

Look, I think I have it now. I know what's wrong.

They miss their babies.

Yeah! When they first came here, the, uh... the bastard hunters that... abandoned them said they left the babies behind.

If we're going to save them from a life of misery, if we're going to save those babies, <under his breath> and turn a tidy profit, we've got to get them some new babies!

passages.title: New Babies
passages.text:
Look, I know these things can be stubborn, but it's all going to be worth it in the end.

Trust me.

passages.title: New Babies
passages.text:
You did it, <name>! Mama, papa, and family. It brings a tear to my eye.

Here, take this runty one. Now that I have the whole herd, this one's just an extra mouth to feed and won't fetch anything at market.

passages.title: The Foot of the Fortress
passages.text:
Your forces are at the ready and the scroll is prepared.

It's time for phase two - stealing a nexus crystal from a fortified ogre compound.

We'll save the scroll to bring in reinforcements in our confrontation with the Gordunni Witch Lord. Let's meet at the base of the Gordal Foothills to head into the fortress proper.

passages.title: The Foot of the Fortress
passages.text: Let's not waste any time. Gordal Fortress awaits just up this hill.

passages.title: While We're in the Neighborhood
passages.text:
Ogres from the empire are known for being cold and calculating.

We are fortunate that their calculations are rarely spot on.

Morkurk has been using enchanted bracelets to empower his minions with arcane strength.

Since we're going to have to dispatch them anyways, we might as well get some reagents out of it.

passages.title: While We're in the Neighborhood
passages.text: Ah, arcane powder. Reminds me of my days as an apprentice.

passages.title: While We're in the Neighborhood
passages.text: They're not amazing, but I do think these have some worth to us.

passages.title: Vicious Viziers
passages.text:
We can't just skate in, kill Witch Lord Morkurk, and leave.

His three lieutenants - Vorgorsh, Zulmork, and Cromaug - are all fiercely loyal to Morkurk, and are all respectable mages in their own right.

I suspect that if we attempt to engage the Witch Lord immediately that they will rush to his aid and overwhelm us. We need to take out his lieutenants first.

passages.title: Vicious Viziers
passages.text: Now that they're out of the way, Morkurk is exposed.

passages.title: Orbs of Power
passages.text:
Minor issue, I'm afraid.

Morkurk has placed powerful wards throughout Gordal Fortress that will prevent any sort of mass summoning - not wonderful considering our plan.

Thankfully, no ogre would ever consider that a single enemy or two would attack, so we should be able to slip through their fortress relatively easily.

passages.title: Orbs of Power
passages.text: Destroying those wards was key to our success. Well done indeed!

passages.title: Dropping In
passages.text:
Witch Lord Morkurk, the leader of the fortress, has catapults set up along the road into their compound.

That won't be a problem for us.

Take out the ogres around the catapults and mark them for me. This vortex spell I have prepared will handle the rest.

We'll meet at the gate to the fortress once the catapults are gone.

passages.title: Dropping In
passages.text: I certainly hope they have more than this to stop us.

passages.title: Dropping In
passages.text: We have the scroll of mass teleportation ready, but we can't use it just yet. We must take proper precautions to ensure our success.

passages.title: Target of Opportunity: Telaar
passages.text:
We've received reports that the draenei enclave at Telaar has fallen to the Warsong.

I sent a small group of shadow hunters to check on the situation.

Kajassa is their leader. Will you meet her there?

passages.title: Target of Opportunity: Telaar
passages.text:
Glad dat Aggra send ya, Commanda.

Dey situation is grim, an' it's 'bout ta get grimma.

passages.title: I Help Ya Kill Dem
passages.text:
Warsong come in an' kill de draenei rangers. No lettin' dem have dis place.

You an' me, Commanda. We gonna kill dem all.

You be distractin' dem an' I usin' me Loa ta finish dem off. You see.

passages.title: I Help Ya Kill Dem
passages.text: Oh, dat was fun. We workin' nicely togetha, you an' me, <name>.

passages.title: Shields Up!
passages.text:
The Warsong packleader is trying to raise Telaar's shield. If Kargora does that, the Warsong will have an impervious base.

So far, they've only managed to initiate the shield. This has the undesirable side effect of protecting the packleader and her shaman at the main crystal.

Activate the crystals on the perimeter of Telaar. That will force the shield to fully deploy.

Once you do that, Kargora will be exposed.

passages.title: Shields Up!
passages.text:
Soon de shield gonna cover all of Telaar. Den we all be trapped inside togetha.

Den we go kill de packleader.

passages.title: Words of the Raven Mother
passages.text:
We came here to perform the ritual of calling to bring the return of the Raven Mother. We had distributed parts of the scroll to everyone and had just begun when we were attacked by the Bloodmane. Now most of the flock has been killed and fragments lay scattered across our homeland.

The ritual was a failure but we will not allow these mongrels to break our faith. We must continue our prayers here but we would be grateful if you can recover the scroll fragments for us.

passages.title: Words of the Raven Mother
passages.text: We must have all the sacred texts! We cannot afford to leave even a single one unaccounted for!

passages.title: Words of the Raven Mother
passages.text:
Ah! The copies of the ritual!

Praise the Raven Mother!

Hand them to me but only one at a time. We must not risk summoning the light.

passages.title: The Bloodmane
passages.text:
We had just arrived and begun the service of the headless fowl when the Bloodmane attacked out of nowhere.

Clearly, this means that the Raven Mother wishes to test the worthiness of her children. Fear not, we are steadfast and will fervently continue our prayers regardless of what may come!

<Sekara leans in and whispers to you.>

Although, if you can get rid of the Bloodmane and their leader that would be a blessing as well.

passages.title: The Bloodmane
passages.text:
Your strength has given us time to rest and continue our rituals.

May the Raven Mother ever keep you in her shadow.

passages.title: The Egg Thieves
passages.text:
The Bloodclaw are sadistic creatures. They have attacked the Ravenskar before and have stolen the eggs of the sacred ravens.

While you are within the Bloodclaw lands keep an eye out for the eggs.

I'll be waiting for you at the nest with as many baskets for them as I can gather.

passages.title: The Egg Thieves
passages.text: Were you able to find the stolen raven eggs?

passages.title: The Egg Thieves
passages.text:
These poor ravens have avoided a horrible future in the Bloodclaw lands.

We will take far better care of them.

Thank you!

passages.title: Get to High Ground!
passages.text:
This dam is about to burst. Hopefully.

Farseer Drek'Thar fights atop the peak to the south of here. You should be safe near him.

Don't worry about me.

passages.title: Guise of the Deceiver
passages.text:
In a cave not far from here, there lives an old woman named Challe.

I knew Challe many years ago when I was young; though as I have become old and grey, she has kept her youth and beauty.

Challe was jealous of my love for Dahaka and I have long suspected that Challe had a part in her death. However, without evidence I could not bring justice against her.

Meet with Challe and tell her that I am dying. Tell her that I wish to know the truth of Dahaka's fate before I leave this world.

passages.title: Guise of the Deceiver
passages.text: I have not much time left. Please, discover the truth of Dahaka's death before it is too late.

passages.title: Guise of the Deceiver
passages.text:
Challe, that iniquitous wretch!

If only I had proof of her treachery long ago, I would have ripped the villainous heart from her chest and crushed it beneath my foot!

You have brought me the truth as I asked, for that you have my thanks.

passages.title: Ralshiara's Demise
passages.text:
It was said in the Journal of the Rising Sun that eating in the mornings cannot be done without harming a few eggs.

The Bloodmane matron, Ralshiara, feasts upon sacred raven eggs for her snacks. How dare she! She must die for her sins!

Take the path south over the mountains to reach the accursed home of the Bloodmane.

Take this trinket, it fell to us from the heavens as a sign of the Raven Mother's favor and with it you might have a chance.

passages.title: Ralshiara's Demise
passages.text:
Let it be known that on this day the stranger has returned victorious from slaying the feared foe of the Flock!

Praise the Raven Mother!

passages.title: Declawing The Bloodmane
passages.text:
It is written in the Scroll of Sermons to "Bite the claw that strikes you."

Take the path south from here that leads over the mountain to the Bloodmane valley in the west. There you will find those of their tribe who can use a primitive form of magic. Slay them and remove their paws.

Once you have obtained a few bring them back to me in the nest so that they may be offered to the Raven Mother!

passages.title: Declawing The Bloodmane
passages.text:
It is written in the Scroll of Sermons that the Raven Mother is not patient, and neither am I.

Do you have the paws of the Bloodmane for me?

passages.title: Declawing The Bloodmane
passages.text: Yes, these will do nicely as an offering to the Raven Mother! May she feast upon our enemies!

passages.title: Back from Beyond
passages.text:
We must begin preparations for the Talon King's return.

From within this realm, I can travel quickly to Veil Terokk.

You, however, should be returned to the other side. You are powerful, and will attract unwanted attention.

passages.title: Back from Beyond
passages.text: Excellent work. Ishaal and Zellek have already begun the rites.

passages.title: An Old Friend
passages.text:
Since the beginning, a shaman has been called to serve the Throne of Elements as its keeper. It is a lifelong calling and a new keeper is only called after the last has passed on.

Gar'rok has been our loyal keeper for many years, cleansing the Elemental Plateau during countless cycles of rebirth.

Our keeper is dying, and soon another will be called in his place. When he passes, he should not be alone. Go to him, <name>.

Ease his pain.

passages.title: An Old Friend
passages.text:
Kalandrios sent you to me? I am honored.

The furies are wise, they know the burdens of my heart.

You may not know, but you have been sent to grant a last request to a dying shaman.

For this, I am grateful.

passages.title: A Flock of Fledglings
passages.text: [PH] asdf

passages.title: Shredder Manual
passages.text:
Hey! I hear there's a curious object nearby. Scouts say it's some kind of shredder manual.

Go check it out for me, will ya? I wonder if it has to do with this new prototype I've been hearin' about...

passages.title: Shredder Manual
passages.text: These orders appear to have come from Orgrim Doomhammer.

passages.title: Shredder Manual
passages.text:
I've been hearing rumors of this new prototype shredder the Iron Horde's engineers have been working on.

I think we ought to investigate. A shadow hunter spotted some sort of shredder manual, and it might have something to do with that prototype.

passages.title: Shredder Manual
passages.text: These orders appear to have come from Orgrim Doomhammer.

passages.title: Dreadpiston
passages.text:
Nearby, a group of Iron Horde took over a key strategic position with surprising alacrity.

They used a machine they call Dreadpiston to terrible effect in the siege, and I believe we need to destroy that machine before moving against the Iron Horde in Tuurem.

passages.title: Dreadpiston
passages.text: An infernal machine.

passages.title: They Call Him Lantresor of the Blade
passages.text:
The Burning Blade clan at Hallvalor is supplying the Warsong with weapons and warriors. We cannot let this continue.

There's a young blademaster who's been exiled from the Burning Blade for many years. They call him Lantresor of the Blade.

My rangari recently saw him return to Hallvalor to challenge the blademaster leadership. Instead, they clapped him in chains.

Maybe he's still alive. Maybe he'll help you deal with the Burning Blade.

passages.title: They Call Him Lantresor of the Blade
passages.text:
Who are you?

Don't you know death by sight, <class>?

passages.title: The Friend o' My Enemy
passages.text:
Hallvalor is the ancestral home o' the Burning Blade clan. Since they be such fast friends, the Warsong allow the blademasters an' their shaman to remain in Nagrand when all o' the other clans are forced out.

Blah, blah, blah.

I say, if they're the friend o' my enemy, then they're my enemy, and that's all I need to know!

passages.title: The Friend o' My Enemy
passages.text:
You done us a solid with them Burning Blade, lad, and we're not the forgettin' kind.

Let's celebrate o'er a pint in an hour. Drinks are on me.

passages.title: Blood of the Burning Blade
passages.text:
Hallvalor is the ancestral home of my clan, the Burning Blade. When the new warlord and his family came to power, I was exiled for being a half-breed.

I want justice.

I suspect you won't mind killing along the way. Not that you'll have any choice.

passages.title: Blood of the Burning Blade
passages.text:
You done us a solid with them Burning Blade, lad, and we're not the forgettin' kind.

Let's celebrate o'er a pint in an hour. Drinks are on me.

passages.title: The Blade Itself
passages.text:
When they clapped me in irons, the Burning Blade instructor, Luhk the Keen-Eyed, took my blade. He's an honorable orc, even if his training techniques are counter-productive.

I want my blade back, <class>.

passages.title: The Blade Itself
passages.text: A blademaster without a blade is no blademaster at all.

passages.title: The Blade Itself
passages.text: If you can defeat Luhk, then perhaps there's some hope for you after all.

passages.title: Meet Me in the Cavern
passages.text: It's time, <class>. Time to face the masters.

passages.title: Meet Me in the Cavern
passages.text:
You made it. Good.

Getting in here was nothing compared to what's to come.

passages.title: Dreadpiston
passages.text:
The Iron Horde overtook a peaceful draenei outpost without mercy.

They used a machine they call Dreadpiston to level the town in minutes.

Destroy it.

passages.title: Dreadpiston
passages.text: They will not use that machine to kill any more draenei. Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: The Land Provides
passages.text: The icevines of the Shivering Trench have developed a powerful resistance to cold temperatures. Integrating them into the construction materials of the garrison should prove useful.

passages.title: The Land Provides
passages.text: Look at you, bein' all resourceful.

passages.title: The Land Provides
passages.text: Now this is some handy stuff. This weather has been cutting through our supplies of rope so quick we need something we can use to provide an alternative. Looks like you scored the jackpot.

passages.title: Khadgar's Plan
passages.text:
We have the Iron Horde backed into a corner now, thanks to you.

It is almost time to enter the city of Shattrath and repel them.

First, we must meet Khadgar and some new allies.

passages.title: Khadgar's Plan
passages.text: You have done great work with Durotan, Draka, and Gazlowe.

passages.title: Khadgar's Plan
passages.text:
Shattrath must not fall into the hands of the Iron Horde. It is time again for me to get my hands bloody.

We will tell Khadgar we are ready to enter the city and take back what is rightfully ours.

passages.title: Khadgar's Plan
passages.text: You have done great work with Maraad, Yrel, and Thaelin.

passages.title: The Farseer Awaits
passages.text:
Your presence has been requested at the Throne of Elements, <name>.

Farseer Drek'Thar heard the call of the furies upon the wind and made the journey to commune with the elements.

The Farseer has sent word that you are to join him at the Throne of Elements.

Go and see what the elements would have of you.

passages.title: The Farseer Awaits
passages.text: Throm-Ka, <name>. All is not right in Nagrand, it is good that you are here.

passages.title: Called to the Throne
passages.text:
It was not long after I arrived in Nagrand that the voice of Kalandrios called out to me upon the wind.

It is a great honor to be called to the Throne of Elements, but my heart was heavy sensing the purpose.

There is dark malaise in the air, it can be felt all around us. It surrounds all life here...enveloping...smothering...

Come, it is time we commune with the furies and lend them our aid. An invisible shadow has been cast upon this valley and it may be up to us to remove it.

passages.title: Called to the Throne
passages.text: It is time that we communed with the furies regarding the sickness here.

passages.title: Called to the Throne
passages.text:
I fear that this disturbance is more dire than I had anticipated.

Whatever it is...it threatens to unravel the elemental bonds that hold this world together.

passages.title: The Only Way to Travel
passages.text:
Call me cautious but I kept a few flares just in case we needed to evac.

I'm glad that wasn't needed but we could still use the ride back to the arsenal.

Are you ready, <sir/ma'am>?

passages.title: The Only Way to Travel
passages.text: The outpost is now fully up and running and we have enough material to outfit an army - your army!

passages.title: Dropping Bombs
passages.text:
The Gordunni have only a single path to their fortress and it is well-defended from a large attack.

Thankfully they wont be expecting just the two of us to be attempting to break in.

This is a great opportunity to take out their defenses and get some target practice for our gunners back at the artillery tower.

Take these smoke grenades and use it to call in an artillery strike on their catapults as we head up.

passages.title: Dropping Bombs
passages.text: Now that we're inside we have much to do.

passages.title: Supply Recovery
passages.text:
We seem to have arrived at just the right time!

The Gordunni have been enchanting armaments for the Iron Horde and it looks like they haven't picked up the latest shipment.

We could put that gear to far better use in our artillery tower! Lets go hunt down their shipping containers. I brought some signal flares that we can use to call in an air pick-up when we've secured the shipment.

passages.title: Supply Recovery
passages.text:
Alright, that should be the last one we need. 

It isn't the same as retaking Shattrath, but knowing the Iron Horde won't be getting these supplies gives me a bit of satisfaction.

passages.title: Punching Through
passages.text:
To secure the fortress we need to kill Witch Lord Morkurk, but I don't think we should go straight after him.

His three lieutenants - Vorgorsh, Zulmork, and Cromaug - are all powerful mages, and all of them are fiercely loyal to Morkurk.

I suspect that if we engage the Witch Lord that they will rush to his aid. Let's take them out so that cannot happen.

passages.title: Punching Through
passages.text: We need to make sure those Vizier's are taken care of before we can deal with Morkurk.

passages.title: Punching Through
passages.text:
Now with the viziers gone the whole Gordunni enchantment trade with the Iron Horde will come crashing down!

We can now turn our attention to dealing with Morkurk.

passages.title: The Only Way to Travel
passages.text:
Call me cautious but I kept a few flares just in case we needed to quickly escape.

I'm glad that wasn't needed but we could still use the ride back to the artillery tower.

Are you ready <sir/ma'am>?

passages.title: The Only Way to Travel
passages.text: The outpost is now fully up and running and we have enough material to outfit an army - your army!

passages.title: Forever Young
passages.text:
All this sitting around is horrible for business.

I have to find a way to recoup some of my lost profits.

Those Draenei females are obsessed with the way their horns look.

I overheard one of them talking about a root that grows in Blademoon Bloom that supposedly reduces horn shedding or something.

I bet I could sell that root to them for a pretty nice profit.

I'll give you a cut if you help me get a supply going.

passages.title: Forever Young
passages.text: Did you find any Youngroot?

passages.title: Forever Young
passages.text:
Hmm... How am I going to package this?

I have an idea!

<Beezil writes Youngroot on a label and slaps it onto a bottle of adder oil.>

< He throws the Youngroot in the bushes behind him.>

Perfect!

passages.title: Botani Beatdown
passages.text:
Gidwin is doing much better. Thank you, <name>.

I can't believe the draenei have lived alongside those horrible monsters for so long.

Maybe we should show these beasts what happens when you mess with an Azerothian.

passages.title: Botani Beatdown
passages.text: That's what I'm talking about! Great work out there, <name>.

passages.title: Rotting Riverbeasts
passages.text:
The botani are infecting the local riverbeasts with some kind of strange flesh-eating plant.

I fear this infection could spread to our people.

If you see any infested riverbeasts, kill the blooming plants that inhabit their bodies... before they kill you.

passages.title: Rotting Riverbeasts
passages.text: We need to stop this infestation.

passages.title: Rotting Riverbeasts
passages.text: This new is disturbing to say the least. I'm shocked the infestation has spread so quickly.

passages.title: Slumberbloom
passages.text:
Huh?... Oh my, I appear to have fallen asleep again.

These slumberblooms are nothing but trouble. One second I'm fighting botani and the next I'm dreaming I'm an elekk dancing with riverbeasts.

*Yawn* We really should do something about all these slumberbloo *Yawn* ... ZZZZzzzzzzzz

<You gather a small handful of pebbles laying by the sleeping draenei.>

passages.title: Hatred Undying
passages.text:
The blood of the dead god, Sethe, lingers in the pools here. And with it, his hatred of Rukhmar and Anzu.

So strong was this hate that it animates the blood even now, eons after he was slain by his fellow gods.

I need the congealed blood that holds those spiteful creatures together.

There is nothing the Adherents fear more than the power of this curse - what if we could brandish it against them?

passages.title: Hatred Undying
passages.text:
My attempts to bottle the pooled blood have failed. It breaks down and dissipates when it is taken away from Sethe's bones.

But I have high hopes for this congealed form!

passages.title: Hatred Undying
passages.text: Excellent, excellent. Go ahead and drop those directly into the cauldron.

passages.title: Banished From the Sky
passages.text:
The Adherents have been casting their enemies into the hollow for generations.

The pools carry Sethe's dying curse, crippling arakkoa with visions of darkness and intense pain. The mind reels, the body writhes, and the wings wither.

Most arakkoa die or go insane. Only the strongest can resist - seek them out and use the Eye of Anzu to help them to their senses.

Beware, for the worshippers of Sethe also prey on these survivors to fill their ranks.

passages.title: Banished From the Sky
passages.text: They have suffered a fate worse than death, but at least they are free.

passages.title: Gaze of the Raven God
passages.text:
The Sethekk are breeding vile wind serpents from Sethe's blood and bones. With these creatures, they will tear apart the sky.

The nests are protected by powerful magic, but Anzu's gaze should penetrate them with ease.

Let us visit the nests and destroy them!

passages.title: Gaze of the Raven God
passages.text: <As the orb meets the altar, the nearby candles flare up.>

passages.title: Sons of Sethe
passages.text:
Many years have passed since anyone has been in contact with Anzu. He faded away, as Terokk did, to take refuge in the shadows.

If we are to coax him back, we should make an offering.

Sethe took the sky from us all - it seems fitting to take the wings of his children.

passages.title: Sons of Sethe
passages.text: <A large bowl awaits an offering for the raven god.>

passages.title: Sons of Sethe
passages.text: <Heaping the wings into the bowl, you hear a faint rustling of feathers from somewhere overhead.>

passages.title: Poison Paralysis
passages.text:
There are others from the caravan that have gone missing.

My guess is they have been taken into Blademoon Bloom by the botani.

You have to rescue them, <name>. You are our only hope.

Here, take some of this elixir I just made, chances are you will need it.

passages.title: Poison Paralysis
passages.text:
I can never repay you for all you have done here today, <name>.

I am truly in your debt.

passages.title: Rendezvous with the Ritualists
passages.text:
Our dear brother Sekara went to the Ravenskar with some of the flock to enact the great ritual of purification.

No one has been sent back to the nest for supplies in the past day; caught up in prayers I suppose.

I would go check on him but I need to make sure the scribe didn't mess up her transcription of my latest sermon. Could you do it? I'll be there in... well, who knows...

passages.title: Rendezvous with the Ritualists
passages.text: At last, our prayers to the Raven Mother have been answered!

passages.title: UNUSED
passages.text: [PH] Now that we're somewhat safer and the texts are returned go report back to the High Ravencaller. We will continue our prayers here.

passages.title: Call of the Raven Mother
passages.text:
All is now in its place to begin the ritual of calling that will bring the Raven Mother back to the nest.

You have fulfilled all of the tests we have put before you so it is only fitting that you join with us and participate in the ritual.

Soon the Raven Mother herself will appear before us! Oh my feathers are tingling in excitement!

Speak to me again when you are ready.

passages.title: Call of the Raven Mother
passages.text:
You have done much to help my little nest of forgotten ones. The poor creatures are not quite sane but with their own kin hunting them I pity their plight.

Their flying kin, the Adherents you call them, would see the forgotten ones destroyed and my children made into slaves.

This I must not allow!

passages.title: The High Ravenspeaker
passages.text:
Yes, I knew you were worthy!

The Writ of Faith says that great doubt will come in time of crisis but one must put their trust in the Raven Mother and all will be as it should!

Come, come, we must go to the High Ravenspeaker!

passages.title: The High Ravenspeaker
passages.text:
In the whispers of the Raven Mother, blessed she be, it was foretold in the Scroll of Order that upon calling for a sign that we would receive one within thirty minutes or less.

This is most fortunate, for we have already begun our preparations for her arrival and we have need of your assistance.

passages.title: The False Talon King
passages.text:
Ikiss was once a respected sage among the Adherents, but his search for the truth of Terokk's fall led to his own banishment.

Ikiss became obsessed with Terokk, even claiming to be the old hero reborn. He commands the Sethekk, promising untold power in a new age of darkness.

Know this: Ikiss is no Talon King. Slay the delusional fool, and search him for anything useful. He is known to collect powerful trinkets.

passages.title: The False Talon King
passages.text: Have you silenced the false king?

passages.title: The False Talon King
passages.text: A bracelet? Interesting... rather plain looking...

passages.title: Sethe, the Dead God
passages.text:
The time has come to put an end to Sethe. I killed him before, and with your help I shall do it again.

Ready yourself for a fight - the cultists will not stand idly by while we stamp out their god.

passages.title: Sethe, the Dead God
passages.text: Sethe has died twice, but his curse lives on. It seems we will never be rid of it.

passages.title: Lithic's Gift
passages.text:
<Kurekk squints at the bangle, rotating it slowly in his claws.>

There is an inscription on the inside.

"To my father, may Rukhmar illuminate your path. With love, Lithic."

It cannot be... This is Terokk's bangle! It was a gift from his daughter, he wore it for years until...

Well, we had better return it.

Terokk built a memorial to Lithic not far from Talon Watch. It should rest there.

passages.title: Lithic's Gift
passages.text: Who... are you? Why have you stirred me?

passages.title: Lithic's Gift
passages.text:
That bracelet... I made it for father long ago.

Before the fall...

passages.title: Blademoon Bloom
passages.text:
We are out of options.

I'm going into the bloom to find out what's going on. I'll meet you inside.

Goodluck, <class>.

passages.title: Blademoon Bloom
passages.text: Good, you made it. I need your help.

passages.title: Gestating Genesaur
passages.text:
This is bad. A genesaur is starting to sprout right here in the bloom.

This is the first reported case of a genesaur being born in draenor in over three hundred years.

No wonder the botani have been acting so crazy. They are bringing back bodies to fertilize that monstrosity.

We have to kill it before it gets any larger. Once fully grown there is no stopping that beast.

passages.title: Gestating Genesaur
passages.text: I never thought I would see a genesaur in my lifetime.

passages.title: Gestating Genesaur
passages.text:
That was close.

If that genesaur would have grown any larger we would have needed an army to destroy it.

Thank you for all your help.

passages.title: Basic Skulltaking
passages.text:
My hunters are all dead, you will be my hunting pack now.

Find their bodies and take their skulls. I will choose which to honor and which to cast aside. It is our way.

I will go further and see what other skulls may be found here.

passages.title: Basic Skulltaking
passages.text: Afraid to get your hands dirty?  They are just bodies now, no need to be scared.

passages.title: Basic Skulltaking
passages.text: This red slime covers everything, even the skulls of my hunters!  I'll make a Skulltaker of you yet though, great work!

passages.title: Skulltaker's Revenge
passages.text: The others... gone or wandered into the haze. It called to me as well but I am too strong. I chose to kill until they crushed my body. I haven't killed enough of them yet adventurer, not enough! Go. Kill more of them and tell my hunt leader that I don't go alone into the dark.

passages.title: Skulltaker's Revenge
passages.text: Hah!  If he was that strong he'd still be alive.  Still it is good you did him honor.  Did you take his skull by any chance?

passages.title: Mysterious Pod
passages.text: This pod is similar to the ones growing on or near the bodies around here, except this one is pulsating weirdly. Grulkor might know more about this.

passages.title: Mysterious Pod
passages.text: What's this?  Let me check if it has a skull...

passages.title: Lighting The Darkness
passages.text:
The spirits of my ancestors have always been drawn to the mountain of Oshu'gun. Now, I too feel this pull deep within my soul...but something is not right.

The presence that beckons us has grown dark and ominous. It consumes the souls of the dead, the souls of my ancestors, <name>.

Something must be done.

Take hold of the spirit torch and light the ceremonial pyres in the Ancestral Grounds.

The flame of the spirit torch upon the pyres will calm the restless spirits being drawn into the void.

passages.title: Lighting The Darkness
passages.text:
Now that the flame of the spirit torch is upon the pyres, the spirits of my ancestors have been insulated from the call of the void within Oshu'gun.

However, more must still be done if the spirits here are to rest peacefully.

passages.title: Echoes of the Past
passages.text:
When a spirit is consumed by the void, an echo of the soul is all that is left behind.

Neither in the physical or spiritual sense of the word would these echoes be considered 'alive.' The echo is merely a twisted reverberation of the anguish left behind by the soul as it is consumed.

If left unchecked, the echoes will lash out against the living and stir the spirits of the dead from their graves.

In order to restore peace to the Ancestral Grounds, these echoes must be put to rest.

passages.title: Echoes of the Past
passages.text:
Do not mourn the twisted echoes of the dead, they are merely the distorted reflections of once noble spirits.

Instead, mourn the loss of those souls consumed by the dark void that grows within Oshu'gun.

passages.title: We Have Company
passages.text:
Outsider, I've spotted Iron Horde soldiers nearby.

It is bold, even for them, to venture into such deadly territory.

If you do not deal with their presence, they will surely be a threat to your camp.

passages.title: We Have Company
passages.text:
Thank you, friend. I am in your debt.

This arrogant Iron Horde has made a dangerous enemy today.

passages.title: The Secret of the Fungus
passages.text:
It smells here and there are whispers.

I feel there is a connection between the plants and beasts here. Special mushrooms seem to focus the beasts' attention.

Go and get some of these for me. I... need... them.

passages.title: The Secret of the Fungus
passages.text: Where are my mushrooms?!

passages.title: The Secret of the Fungus
passages.text: Yes, they smell... wonderful. These will help me find the power of this marsh and take it for my own.

passages.title: A Grim Harvest
passages.text: The larger monsters are the key to my destiny, I can feel it. The pods growing on them are even bigger than the one you brought me earlier. Get me a few of these, they will be... helpful... soon.

passages.title: A Grim Harvest
passages.text: I need more of those pods!  Many more!

passages.title: A Grim Harvest
passages.text: These will aid me greatly.  I must consume them and take their power.  We are close to the end <name>, I can feel it.

passages.title: A Heartfelt Search
passages.text: I can feel a powerful presence in the marsh adventurer. I feel drawn to it. We must go and take what is there. Go on ahead, I must finish consuming these mushrooms.

passages.title: A Heartfelt Search
passages.text: We are so close I can almost touch it!  We will have to go deeper, much deeper!

passages.title: Welcome to Gorgrond
passages.text:
Gorgrond is one of the most untamed landscapes in all of Draenor.

Only the most skilled of rangari venture this deep into the wilds.

It is their camp we are heading for. If you wish to travel ahead, it can be found down this path and to the right.

Maraad and I shall follow after you momentarily. We still have some logistics to work out before we leave the landing.

passages.title: Welcome to Gorgrond
passages.text: I am a fan of the temple gardens but this place is just too far gone for my tastes.

passages.title: Welcome to Gorgrond
passages.text: You have chosen a very unfortunate time to visit our camp, my friend.

passages.title: Seedbearers of Bad News
passages.text:
When these seedbearers are slain their seeds survive. From them spring new seedbearers, not over years, but hours.

Leaving their remains here would soon cause your camp to be overrun.

Burn them, outsider, if you wish your camp to endure.

passages.title: Seedbearers of Bad News
passages.text: Watch them burn!

passages.title: Is This One of Yours?
passages.text:
I found this one skulking nearby. He claims to be an ally of yours.

Is this true? Or does he cook slowly over my fire?

passages.title: Is This One of Yours?
passages.text: That half-orc burned my toes!

passages.title: Xuk It!
passages.text:
It is done.

With this enchantment, not only can you roam amongst the goren freely, but you can move as they do.

Your travels through Gorgrond are now made simple. You have safe access to places otherwise impossible to reach.

Xuk's ancestors have made it so.

passages.title: Xuk It!
passages.text: What has that orc done to you?!

passages.title: Xuk It!
passages.text: It is good that you still have your wits about you. You do... have your wits about you?

passages.title: In Ared's Memory
passages.text:
My master has gone on to the Light, but I will continue his work.

<Miall looks to Ared >

Shanai ortar, Ared.

I will have his body sent to Auchindoun. For now, show me this artillery tower of yours.

passages.title: In Ared's Memory
passages.text:
This is a beautiful and well equipped structure. Thank you for allowing me to work here.

I am positive with this place I can carry on my master's legacy. You will not regret this!

passages.title: Lost Mole Machines
passages.text:
Few people know the Blackrock clan better than Dark Iron dwarves.

So after Tanaan, we sent a bunch of mole machines to Gorgrond to build a listenin' post to keep an eye on them.

Me own mole machine got way off course an' I got separated. It didn't take long to figure out all the other mole machines got off course as well.

Accordin' to the readin's in me tank, a mole machine surfaced somewhere way to the west of here.

Mind scoutin' ahead while we get this tank operational?

passages.title: Lost Mole Machines
passages.text: I came here to fight the Blackrock clan, not get lost in the jungle.

passages.title: Lost Mole Machines
passages.text: Well, that's one down, and about a dozen others to go. We best get a base goin'. Sounds like we might be here a while.

passages.title: The Mysterious Flask
passages.text:
The liquid swirling around inside the flask clearly has strong alchemical properties, but its nature is beyond your training.

You have heard that one of the Stonefang refugees at your garrison has some knowledge of the alchemy of Draenor. Perhaps he could tell you more?

passages.title: The Mysterious Flask
passages.text: Ah. I see you have found a creation of Draenor alchemy.

passages.title: Along the Riverside
passages.text:
Vindicator Yrel has taken most of our forces north. She's establishing a forward base along the Skysong River.

She'll want to know that we're almost ready to move against Grommashar.

I'm sure she can also use your help dealing with the Warsong orcs at Lok-rath.

passages.title: Along the Riverside
passages.text:
It's good to see you, commander. When I'd heard about your garrison caravan being destroyed....

Well, let's just say that I feared the worst.

What word from Telaari Station?

passages.title: Terms of Surrender
passages.text:
Believe it or not, I have good news: we've already taken Lok-rath.

<The vindicator beams with pride.>

Our soldiers have captured most of the Warsong, including their leader, Uruk Foecleaver.

I saved the honor of accepting his surrender for you. They're waiting for you inside, commander.

passages.title: Terms of Surrender
passages.text:
Commander <name>.

Terms of surrender? Hmm... let me think.

passages.title: Lok-rath is Secured
passages.text:
With their leader dead, the remaining Warsong will be easier to finish.

As soon as that's done, I'll pull our soldiers out of Lok-rath and head for Grommashar.

If you're heading back to Telaari Station, would you please inform D'kaan?

passages.title: Lok-rath is Secured
passages.text:
If you hadn't gone to Lok-rath, our forces would have been decimated.

I'm sorry to hear they laid a trap for you. I guess you have a reputation now.

passages.title: We Need An Outpost
passages.text:
Commander, we've gathered enough materials to build an outpost that will support our mission against the Iron Horde.

How shall we proceed?

A lumber yard would be valuable for gathering resources in the dense overgrowth to the south, and in confronting the plant monstrosities that defend it.

On the other hand, a sparring arena would provide us the brutish forces we'd need to push through the magnaron wastelands to the north.

When you're ready, make your choice on the table.

passages.title: We Need An Outpost
passages.text: Buildin' an outpost out here requires a certain kind o' crazy.

passages.title: We Need An Outpost
passages.text: Well, that is one thing ta pick. Tell you what, you get this building up and running at full steam and I'll see if I can't adapt these blueprints to work for the space in your garrison.

passages.title: A Harvester Has Come
passages.text:
This is what happens when one stands in the path of a genesaur. And where a genesaur walks, the botani follow.

I saw one entering our shelter cave along the northern side of the camp.

It is commanding the podlings to gather the corpses of our fallen brethren and must be stopped.

I must tend to our wounded, and gather supplies for our departure.

If you are serious about being a hero, venture into the cave and slay this botani.

passages.title: A Harvester Has Come
passages.text: I dread to think what the botani had intended to do with the corpses of our fallen.

passages.title: Silence the War Machines
passages.text:
The Iron Horde supplied Lok-rath with war machines from Ironfist Harbor. It won't take long for them to level Yrel's Watch.

Someone has to silence those war machines!

passages.title: Silence the War Machines
passages.text: Thank you, commander. I thought we were done for sure.

passages.title: Terror of Nagrand
passages.text:
<The body of a fallen soldier lies here. Blood and gore trail back from the corpse to the entrance of the cave just to the north.>

<Judging by the howls and the carnage surrounding the den, something truly terrifying must be in there.>

passages.title: Terror of Nagrand
passages.text: Commander. How may I help you?

passages.title: Terror of Nagrand
passages.text: That's the beast's collar? I heard its howls all the way over here!

passages.title: Spore-be-Gone
passages.text:
We got an emergency!

A bunch of spore drifters have infested the shore and tore up our Spore-B-Gone turrets.

We're caught with our armor off here! If we don't get those turrets back online then those spores are going to float right in to town and then we'll have another Pinchwhistle Point on our hands!

We need to get out there and manually activate them.

Well? Are you in?

passages.title: Spore-be-Gone
passages.text:
Hey you got the dispensers going again.

Nice job pal!

passages.title: The Mother Lode
passages.text:
Hey we got ourselves a crisis here! Our zeppelin "The Mother Lode" crashed onto the south mountain range.

It was supposed to only be on an observation mission, what could have happened?

We got to get down there quick and I'm going to need your help on this.

Are you with me?

passages.title: The Mother Lode
passages.text:
Oh my gosh, this is way worse than I thought it was gonna be. I'm really going to need a hand with getting these survivors out of here.

Good thing I have you on the payroll.

passages.title: Clearing Out Before Cleaning Up
passages.text:
Here's the situation.

We need to get this salvage operation moving ASAP, but the ship went down right in the middle of the wasp nests.

The ugly bugs are all over the place, and I can't call my team in here to start work until they're taken care of.

Go kill as many of 'em as you can and I'll cut you in on some of the haul.

passages.title: Clearing Out Before Cleaning Up
passages.text:
I still see a mess of wasps down there.

We need to clear those wasps out before I can get the salvage operation started.

passages.title: Clearing Out Before Cleaning Up
passages.text:
That's how ye do it! As soon as my crew gets here we can start work.

Here's your pay. Thanks for doing the job.

passages.title: Getting the Crew Back Together
passages.text:
