Oh wow, the debris is all over the mountainside! The survivors won't make it if we don't do something quick. They need healing NOW!

Here, take my bandages and go patch them up.

passages.title: Getting the Crew Back Together
passages.text:
Good work, <name>.

Once Gazwitz gets his team up here we can get the crewmen back to the Gearworks.

passages.title: Disrupt the Rituals
passages.text:
No longer do the Warsong seek to be one with the elements; instead they abuse their power by using it to channel the darkness of the void.

I will not tolerate these rituals to continue. Locate the ritual totems the Warsong use to channel the void and destroy them.

The gift of the elements was not given to the orcs only to be defiled and used as a plaything.

passages.title: Disrupt the Rituals
passages.text: Have you destroyed the ritual totems?

passages.title: Disrupt the Rituals
passages.text:
Dark shamanism is a dangerous practice, <name>.

It is true that the void can be a source of terrible power, but it is the kind of power that comes at a price.

These woods are safer now that you have put an end to the rituals.

passages.title: Through the Nether
passages.text:
The rituals have been disrupted, yet the nether beacons still glow with power....

This can only mean that the beacons are powered from within the Twisting Nether itself!

The connection to the void must be severed! There is but one way to accomplish this; you must slay the void creature that maintains the connection with our world.

Lay your hands upon a beacon and travel into the Twisting Nether. When you have arrived on the other side, locate a Shamanstone and use it to contact me.

passages.title: Through the Nether
passages.text: The veil between dimensions is thin. Do you hear my words through the shaman stone?

passages.title: Through the Nether
passages.text:
The Shamanstone appears to be working, even from within the Twisting Nether.

There is much that needs to be done, <name>. The monsters of the void are gathering upon Oshu'gun and must be stopped, else they invade our realm.

passages.title: The Void March
passages.text:
Hidden behind the veil of the Twisting Nether, the abominations of the void march upon Oshu'gun. The great void growing deep within the mountain has drawn them like moths to a flame.

Wave upon wave, the creatures of the void march upon the mountain and sacrifice themselves to Invalidus. The void lord Invalidus cannot be allowed to feast upon the other void creatures, else it will become too powerful to stop.

passages.title: The Void March
passages.text: The void lord must be stopped. Thanks to your effort, the tide of void creatures has waned... but if we are to defeat Invalidus we must act swiftly.

passages.title: The Nether Approaches
passages.text:
By connecting with the Twisting Nether, the Warsong shaman have created a ripple effect that they could not have anticipated.

Look around and you will see countless portals beginning to open, signs that the Twisting Nether seeks to connect to Draenor.

Should these portals successfully open, the path will be clear for all manner of demons and void creatures to rampage across this valley.

passages.title: The Nether Approaches
passages.text:
If those portals were to fully expand and open, the path would have been clear for the horrors of the Twisting Nether to march upon Nagrand.

The Warsong have been careless in their mad pursuit of power and glory.

passages.title: Skimming Off the Top
passages.text:
That flying machine is our ticket out of here but its fuel tank is bone dry!

We're right next to the oil fields but with the infected out there we don't have time to run a line up here so we need to improvise.

The oil creatures moving next to the pumps out there are full of a highly potent mixture that I can drop right into the tank. Grab some of that oil for me and we'll be one step closer to getting out of here.

passages.title: Skimming Off the Top
passages.text: Do ya have that oil for me yet?

passages.title: Skimming Off the Top
passages.text:
Yea that's the stuff!

Now I just need to connect the spark plugs and patch up a few holes and it'll be nearly in working order!

passages.title: Sporicide
passages.text:
It's revolting, absolutely disgusting, infuriating even!

I'm talking about seeing those spore creatures walking around Pinchwhistle Point.

While I'm working on the machine here how about you go out and kill off some of those spore creatures? I'll feel a bit better knowing there are less of those things moving around.

passages.title: Sporicide
passages.text: Did you put down those spore creatures yet?

passages.title: Sporicide
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>.

The less of those spore beasts around the safer we all are.

passages.title: The Portal's Power
passages.text:
The mana bombs were not enough. This was always a risk.

This is unfortunate.

Gul'dan, the orc beneath these grates, says he can shut down this portal. Find a way in there, and do whatever it takes to slow this portal down.

<The archmage's eyes lock with yours.>

WHATEVER IT TAKES.

passages.title: The Dark Side of the Moon
passages.text:
Yrel and I have located Warlord Ner'zhul. He is meeting with Grommash Hellscream atop the highest altar overlooking Anguish Fortress.

Meet us there. We must stop him.

passages.title: The Dark Side of the Moon
passages.text: Ner'zhul will pay for what he has done.

passages.title: The Dark Side of the Moon
passages.text:
We saved everyone we could, <name>. We were too late for the others... including my sister.

Prophet Velen is right. When it is asked of us, we ALL must fight. I promise this: I will never again let my loved ones suffer.

Ner'zhul is close to calling down the Dark Star. We are the only ones who can stop him.

passages.title: A Deal with Darkness
passages.text: <With Gul'dan gone, the Dark Portal is disabled, and the threat to Azeroth is suspended.>

passages.title: Along the Riverside
passages.text:
Durotan has taken most of our forces west. He's establishing a forward base along the Skysong River.

He'll want to know that we're almost ready to move against Grommashar.

I'm sure he'll also appreciate your help dealing with the Warsong orcs at Lok-rath.

passages.title: Along the Riverside
passages.text:
It's good to see you, commander. When I'd heard about your garrison caravan being destroyed....

Well, let's just say that I feared the worst.

What word from Wor'var?

passages.title: Terms of Surrender
passages.text:
I have good news, commander: we've already taken Lok-rath.

<The warchief grins.>

The Horde's soldiers have captured most of the Warsong, including their leader, Uruk Foecleaver.

I saved the honor of accepting his surrender for you. They're waiting for you inside, commander.

passages.title: Terms of Surrender
passages.text:
Commander <name>.

Terms of surrender? Hmm... let me think.

passages.title: Lok-rath is Secured
passages.text:
With their leader dead, the remaining Warsong will be easy pickings.

As soon as that's done, I'll pull our soldiers out of Lok-rath and head for Grommashar.

If you're heading back to Wor'var, inform Thrall that we'll be ready soon.

passages.title: Lok-rath is Secured
passages.text:
If you hadn't gone to Lok-rath, our forces would have been decimated.

I'm sorry to hear they laid a trap you. You have a reputation now.

passages.title: Silence the War Machines
passages.text:
The Iron Horde supplied Lok-rath with war machines from Ironfist Harbor. It won't take long for them to level Riverside Post.

Someone has to silence those war machines!

passages.title: Silence the War Machines
passages.text: Thank you, commander. I thought we were done for sure.

passages.title: Terror of Nagrand
passages.text:
<The body of a fallen soldier lies here. Blood and gore trail back from the corpse to the entrance of the cave just to the north.>

<Judging by the howls and the carnage surrounding the den, something truly terrifying must be in there.>

passages.title: Terror of Nagrand
passages.text: Commander. How may I help you?

passages.title: Terror of Nagrand
passages.text: That's the beast's collar? I heard its howls all the way over here!

passages.title: Unleashed Steel
passages.text:
Thank you... boss.

I won't let you down! I didn't even try to sneak one of those low quality blades here that one of your peons placed right next to the cage. Which by the way was a pretty terrible idea and that thing should be moved before you get anyone less honorable in here.

Enough talk, lets check this place out!

passages.title: Unleashed Steel
passages.text:
We have a lot of basic arms here but I'll get them improved in no time.

Thanks for giving me this chance.

passages.title: The Alchemist
passages.text:
I know a little about alchemy from my cousin Kadar. She is the alchemist at Stonefang Outpost. If you wish to learn more, she is the one with whom to speak.

I only hope she has survived the attack.

passages.title: The Alchemist
passages.text: My apprentice... Inside... (She dies in your arms.)

passages.title: The Apprentice
passages.text: Kadar's last words... Is there someone still inside the hut?

passages.title: The Apprentice
passages.text: She is unconscious and pinned under heavy, broken shelves, but she is still breathing.

passages.title: The Apprentice
passages.text: What... happened? Where is my master?

passages.title: Honor and Remember
passages.text:
So she is dead.

She took me in when I had no one. She taught me everything I know. She gave me everything I have. And now, she is dead.

I owe you my life, stranger, but I wish you had saved hers, not mine. Please, help me bury her.

passages.title: Leave Every Soldier Behind
passages.text:
Hmmm.

The ogron possess something of value to the Iron Horde. I'm sure they're unaware, likely just bored and in need of something to torture.

I'd be inclined to just let them be, it's a fate they deserve. But we can't afford not to follow up on this clue. With any luck, it will help us stop the Iron Horde from turning Gorgrond's most fearsome creatures into weapons.

Try to find this Corporal Thukmar and his notes. We'll meet you there.

passages.title: Leave Every Soldier Behind
passages.text: Again you've done well, friend.

passages.title: Leave Every Soldier Behind
passages.text: We have the notes. Let us see what they reveal about our enemy's strategy.

passages.title: The Sparring Arena
passages.text:
We owe you our freedom, and more. I have spoken to the others, we are willing to return with you to your garrison and teach those pitiful creatures you call "soldiers" how to properly fight.

We will also do our best to impart our knowledge to you, Commander. Should you have need of us when in the wilds of Gorgrond, simply call us.

You may wish to warn Rangari Jonaa of our coming.

passages.title: The Sparring Arena
passages.text: Now that we have the trainers, we can start training your forces to do something other than chop lumber. Heh heh.

passages.title: Eye in the Sky
passages.text:
The notes you recovered tell of a device capable of subjugating even a magnaron.

Ancient legends speak of such artifacts, crafted by the worldbuilders to keep these creatures in check. I had discounted them as silly stories, but if they are true...

<name>, Draenor is doomed.

No army will be able to stop them if they harness this power. We must stop them or die trying.

Here, I shall bind our sight to Nisha and hope she can locate this artifact.

passages.title: Eye in the Sky
passages.text: We are in luck! The artifact is still within reach.

passages.title: Eye in the Sky
passages.text: Good. We know where we must go to acquire the artifact.

passages.title: THAELIN!
passages.text:
That little...!

<Yrel tries to maintain her composure.>

Thaelin Darkanvil sent us a shipment. It was supposed to be engineering parts.

Instead, when we just opened one of the crates, out popped a baby goren. Do you know how destructive those things are?

And, of course, the one baby immediately set about letting all the other ones loose.

Want to help me get some revenge?

passages.title: THAELIN!
passages.text: Did you round them all up?

passages.title: THAELIN!
passages.text:
Outstanding.

<Vindicator Yrel beckons you closer so that the two of you can conspire.>

passages.title: Carrier Has Arrived
passages.text:
We're going to get some payback on that little stinker.

Put the baby goren into one of those carriers and then make a special delivery to Thaelin.

passages.title: Carrier Has Arrived
passages.text:
Wait a minute, <name>... let's be reasonable. I can hear what's in that carrier.

It was just a harmless prank.

Don't do it, please!

Stop!

Don't open that carrier!

passages.title: Blood of the Burning Blade
passages.text:
Hallvalor is the ancestral home of my clan, the Burning Blade. When the new warlord and his family came to power, I was exiled for being a half-breed.

I want justice.

I suspect you won't mind killing along the way. Not that you'll have any choice.

passages.title: Blood of the Burning Blade
passages.text:
A great victory over the Burning Blade!

This Flamebender Ka'graz sounds formidable. We shall have to keep an eye on her and her blademasters.

passages.title: Dark Binding
passages.text:
Even as we speak, the pale within Shadowfall Canyon are enslaving the elements to their will. Many elemental spirits have already been enthralled, and more will follow.

The pale must be stopped and the elementals they enslave set free.

Journey into Shadowfall Canyon and set free those elemental spirits which are not fully enthralled by the pale. As for the elementals already enslaved by the pale, the only mercy we can give them now is to release their bonds through death.

passages.title: Dark Binding
passages.text: Have you freed the elemental spirits of Shadowfall Canyon from the dark bonds of the pale?

passages.title: Dark Binding
passages.text: The pale have been taught by Cho'gall to enslave the elemental spirits of this land. When an elemental is enthralled in this manner, it cannot be reversed even by a Farseer such as myself.

passages.title: The Pale Threat
passages.text:
The Pale are wretched creatures that hide beneath the ground, ever plotting against those who dwell upon the surface. They stalk the Underpale, a twisted and dark cavern beneath Oshu'gun.

If we are to succeed in stopping Cho'gall we must fight our way through their ranks beneath the earth.

Make your way into the cavern, slay the vile creatures within and take out the Pale leader... the one known as Greyseer.

passages.title: The Pale Threat
passages.text:
I have encountered evil in many places, <name>. Even deep within my own soul, I have seen dark shadows of what could be.

However, the evil within the hearts of the Pale defies explanation. It is dark, loathing, and miserable in a way I have never encountered.

passages.title: The Good Doctor
passages.text:
Our expedition biologist has been kidnapped by podlings!

We came to Nagrand to explore, to slay the mightiest of beasts, and test our mettle alongside the great Hemet Nesingwary.

As soon as we arrived, Hemet's hunting prowess was needed to combat the Warsong. Rather than sit around twiddling our thumbs, we decided to continue the expedition!

We were exploring Spiteleaf Thicket when podlings ambushed us! In the chaos, Dr. Hadley Ricard was taken captive.

Please, we can't just leave him there!

passages.title: The Good Doctor
passages.text:
Your timely arrival to rescue me from the podlings was most appreciated!

This research station has seen better days... my equipment and belongings were damaged in the ambush.

However, with your aid, I'm sure we'll be up and running again in no time!

passages.title: Trouble at the Overwatch
passages.text:
Ya know, we sent a couple o' scouts ta check out those big, smelly, 'civilized' ogres at Mar'gok's Overwatch.

Haven't heard from 'em in a bit. Matter o' fact, not since I saved yer bacon up at Telaar.

Have some time ta ride over there and check up on 'em, <boyo/girly>?

passages.title: Trouble at the Overwatch
passages.text: I'm afraid we have some trouble.

passages.title: Trouble at the Overwatch
passages.text:
Yesterday, I sent two of my best scouts to spy on the ogres at Mar'gok's Overwatch.

I haven't heard back from them.

<name>, would you do me the honor of checking on them? I'm sure it's nothing; the Overwatch is a large fortification.

I'd feel better knowing they're okay.

passages.title: Trouble at the Overwatch
passages.text: I'm honored you're here to help, wolf-brother. Things here are worse than we thought.

passages.title: Your Base, Your Choice
passages.text:
You have already constructed an impressive garrison in Frostfire. I believe I should defer this next choice to you.

One region of Gorgrond is rich in resources. A lumber mill could help us make the most of them.

Another region harbors hardened gladiators. A sparring arena would help persuade them to fight for our cause.

Either path will strengthen us as we seek to find and weaken the Iron Horde.

Which do you choose, Commander?

passages.title: Your Base, Your Choice
passages.text: A fine choice. It will need more work before such a structure could be built in your garrison, but this is a start.

passages.title: The Sparring Arena
passages.text:
We owe you our freedom, and more. I have spoken to the others, we are willing to return with you to your garrison and teach those pitiful creatures you call "soldiers" how to properly fight.

We will also do our best to impart our knowledge to you, Commander. Should you have need of us when in the wilds of Gorgrond, simply call us.

You may wish to warn Limbflayer of our coming.

passages.title: The Sparring Arena
passages.text:
Kash'drakor is coming here?! Ha! I once saw him cut through a dozen Laughing Skulls because they had his son.

He is the purist expression of destruction.

passages.title: Things Are Not Goren Our Way
passages.text:
The abandoned mine shaft has been overrun with goren! They seem to be responding to commands from a big one further down in the mine. If you can take him out, the rest will probably retreat.

Once you have those goren cleared out, we can get that mine up and working!

passages.title: Things Are Not Goren Our Way
passages.text: Were you able to take out the leader?

passages.title: Things Are Not Goren Our Way
passages.text: Nice job, <name>! Let's get this mining operation started!

passages.title: Removing the Paper Trail
passages.text: This box is filled with writings and diagrams that oddly resemble research into the nullification of magic. It would be best to ruin these efforts by destroying any research found.

passages.title: Removing the Paper Trail
passages.text: Hey, do you smell smoke?

passages.title: Removing the Paper Trail
passages.text: Burning magical paper smells pretty bad!  Good thinking <name>, keeping these ogres dumb is a solid plan!

passages.title: Obtaining Ogre Offensive Orders
passages.text:
The upper bluff must be really important to the ogres. Two fancy looking ogre mages came down from there and starting ordering all the others around.

Go get those orders and meet up with my scout Dalgorsh on the upper bluff. They will be more useful to him up there.

passages.title: Obtaining Ogre Offensive Orders
passages.text: Don't forget! Get the orders and take 'em to Dalgorsh further in.

passages.title: Obtaining Ogre Offensive Orders
passages.text:
Finally some help! I barely got out alive!

You have some ogre orders? Let me see...

Well that's not good news.

passages.title: Removing the Reinforcements
passages.text:
Its not good adventurer, these smart ogres have got a portal working up there and they are bringing in more ogres from somewhere else.

It looks like it takes a lot of effort to keep it open though. If you take it down I'm guessing they will be delayed quite a while.

passages.title: Removing the Reinforcements
passages.text: Good, hopefully they will give up on making a portal here.

passages.title: Ship Salvage
passages.text:
Commander, we are running low on supplies.

Maybe we can salvage materials from that ship you arrived on?

At the rate folks are coming through the portal we are going to be out of everything by sundown... or moondown?

I'm still getting used to this place.

passages.title: Ship Salvage
passages.text: Supplies are getting really low, commander.

passages.title: Ship Salvage
passages.text:
Wow... with all these supplies, we should be back on track.

We are blessed to have you protecting us, commander.

passages.title: Lost in Nagrand
passages.text:
Hey, <mister/lady>, could you help me?

There's this girl I know. Her name's Olgra. Her and her parents went back to Wor'var yesterday. Only, they never got there and no one's seen them.

If you're heading back out, would you look for her?

She's kinda my girlfriend.

passages.title: Lost in Nagrand
passages.text:
Skytooth! My mama and papa....

<The little girl continues to cry over the corpses of her family.>

passages.title: Consumed by Vengeance
passages.text:
They... they came out of nowhere. From that direction.

<The young girl points vaguely west through her tears.>

They were on their nasty wolves.

Please, commander, my family's honor is at stake. Will you get vengeance for me?

passages.title: Consumed by Vengeance
passages.text: Thank you, commander. You really are the greatest <class> like everyone says!

passages.title: Pale Moonlight
passages.text:
We are getting strange reports of an orc attack on a nearby draenei settlement called Eventide Landing.

I'm hearing these particular orcs are unlike any we have encountered before.

They seem... sickly, and are pale in color.

The locals could use our help, commander. This seems like the perfect opportunity to test our garrison's capabilities.

passages.title: Pale Moonlight
passages.text: Did you see the pale orcs, commander?

passages.title: Pale Moonlight
passages.text:
This is unnerving to say the least.

Those things must have come from underground.

Hopefully we have seen the last of them.

passages.title: Garrison Campaign: The Sargerei
passages.text:
Greetings, <name>.

Archmage Khadgar wishes you to hear an important message.

The draenei suffered a great betrayal when one of their leaders, Exarch Othaar, revealed himself to be working with the Legion.

In the hills above Shadowmoon Valley, Othaar, who now goes by the name Socrethar, gathers new recruits to his cause.

Archmage Modera is in charge of this covert operation, which we need your help carrying out.

Meet her in the field, and she will give you the details.

passages.title: Garrison Campaign: The Sargerei
passages.text: Greetings, <class>. Khadgar told me to expect you.

passages.title: Garrison Campaign: The Sargerei
passages.text:
Greetings, <name>.

Archmage Khadgar wishes you to hear an important message.

The draenei suffered a great betrayal when one of their leaders, Exarch Othaar, revealed himself to be working with the Legion.

In the hills above Shadowmoon Valley, Othaar, who now goes by the name Socrethar, gathers new recruits to his cause.

Archmage Modera is in charge of this covert operation, which we need your help carrying out.

Meet her in the field, and she will give you the details.

passages.title: Garrison Campaign: The Sargerei
passages.text: Greetings, <class>. Khadgar told me to expect you.

passages.title: The Word of Socrethar
passages.text:
The Sargerei follow Socrethar zealously. From what I can gather, he is a persuasive and compelling leader.

Many of the initiates carry books of his writings.

I need you to read these works and report back to me. If we can understand the Sargerei's motivations, perhaps we can undermine them.

I last saw these books near the lake, on a table near the fountain, and in the house near the gardens.

passages.title: The Word of Socrethar
passages.text: I see... Socrethar is purely mad, but his reasoning is logical. No wonder so many draenei are turning to his cause.

passages.title: Shattering the Enemy
passages.text:
While you carry out the pretense of obeying Zamaya's orders, we're going to sabotage the Sargerei under their very noses.

All around this village, you can find Felstorm Crystals. The enemy uses these objects to magnify their power.

Destroy these crystals, and we'll slow their operations.

passages.title: Shattering the Enemy
passages.text: Very good. Our mission continues, undetected.

passages.title: Facing Demons
passages.text:
Time is running out, <name>. The Sargerei have opened a summoning portal on the hill to the west.

I believe they are going to use this portal to bring an army of demons here, to Shadowmoon Valley.

We must stop them before this happens, no matter what the cost. Use this arcane bomb to destroy the portal.

We may blow our cover, but stopping the portal is more important right now.

passages.title: Facing Demons
passages.text: <Mysteriously, Anchorite Laanda is gone. Did something happen here?>

passages.title: Socrethar's Fury
passages.text:
<Upon opening the scroll, you find a message from Anchorite Laanda.>

I write this message hastily. I've been discovered. I'm being taken in front of Socrethar.

You must carry on our mission. I've learned that Soulbinder Zamaya holds a detailed plan of Socrethar's next attack.

She still trusts you, so you should be able to enter the main building. Please, find those plans, <name>!

passages.title: Socrethar's Fury
passages.text: Don't worry about me.

passages.title: Socrethar's Fury
passages.text:
<Anchorite Laanda looks pale. He is not going to make it.>

<name>... thank you for all that you have done.

passages.title: Forging Ahead
passages.text:
<Anchorite Laanda's voice is barely a whisper.>

You must report back... to Khadgar.

Socrethar means to take Shattrath. He will... continue to recruit followers... to his side...

Thank you for... helping me... in my final hour...

Leave me... I would like to rest...

passages.title: Forging Ahead
passages.text:
I see... Socrethar's ambitions begin with Shattrath and Auchindoun, but they do not end there.

Thank you for bringing this information to me, <name>.

I will relay it to Archmage Khadgar immediately.

passages.title: Forging Ahead
passages.text:
<Anchorite Laanda's voice is barely a whisper.>

You must report back... to Khadgar.

Socrethar means to take Shattrath. He will... continue to recruit followers... to his side...

Thank you for... helping me... in my final hour...

Leave me... I would like to rest...

passages.title: Forging Ahead
passages.text:
I see... Socrethar's ambitions begin with Shattrath and Auchindoun, but they do not end there.

Thank you for bringing this information to me, <name>.

I will relay it to Archmage Khadgar immediately.

passages.title: Shells for Xuk
passages.text:
The magics Xuk is weaving will let you perform great acts, but preparations must be made before the spirits will bless us with their power.

Xuk needs many shells from the pesky goren. To gather them, Xuk will share a secret.

Approach their tunnel craters and the goren will pour out. This way, you kill many at once.

passages.title: Shells for Xuk
passages.text: Xuk Xuk.

passages.title: Shells for Xuk
passages.text: Ahh, yes. Xuk is one step closer to performing a miracle.

passages.title: More Materials
passages.text:
Building a garrison is no simple task, and it does not happen without the proper resources.

We need a lot more materials.

If you find anything in the field let me know. We need all the help we can get.

passages.title: Pollen Power
passages.text:
The botani use monstrous insect-like creatures to pollinate their bloom.

The pollen they carry has a number of powerful properties that would be of use to your garrison forces.

If you bring me a reserve of this pollen I should be able to convert it to something of value.

passages.title: Pollen Power
passages.text: Do you have the pollen?

passages.title: Pollen Power
passages.text: Keep this up and we'll make a survivalist out of you yet.

passages.title: Burn the Bodies
passages.text:
You don't understand. Anythin' these plant people don't infest they fatten up and then turn inta mulch.

I say we take out their food source.

These botani got a few corpses lying around that I saw. Might be a good idea to burn those bodies.

Let's find out if they can infest ash.

passages.title: Burn the Bodies
passages.text: If I survive this, I'm gonna get even by becomin' a vegetarian.

passages.title: Burn the Bodies
passages.text: Normally I'm not a violent dwarf, but I ain't about to sit by and get turned into a bush. And I ain't about to let others do the same.

passages.title: Coalpart's Revenge
passages.text:
I'm so full I can't swing an axe even if I had one.

Tell ya what, we got a mutual interest here. I need yer help to get a little vengeance on the big botani at the back of this bloom. In return, I'll point ya in the right direction fer gettin' a secret weapon the botani keep.

passages.title: Coalpart's Revenge
passages.text:
Me mother always said: "Burrian! Eat yer veggies!"

Going to make her proud today.

passages.title: Coalpart's Revenge
passages.text: Me mother always told me to eat me vegetables. I dunna think this is what she had in mind.

passages.title: Dark Iron Down
passages.text:
While you were away our rangari here found more clues leadin' to some of me other friends.

Burrian Coalpart and Scorchbrow.

Problem is, their trail heads right for Evermorn Springs to the west.

Please Commander, will ya get in there and save them from mulching?

passages.title: Dark Iron Down
passages.text:
Ah! It was terrible! They made me eat an' eat an' eat.

Don' get me wrong, I enjoy a good meal but these plant people had me eatin' nuthin' but fruit.

I canno' take it anymore.

passages.title: A Great Escape
passages.text:
A goren tunnel!

Once the cap is cleared, it's certain to lead outside of this Light-forsaken pit.

passages.title: A Great Escape
passages.text: Those goren tunnels have proven useful.

passages.title: Deeproot
passages.text:
Since yer all set up to take on trees and bushes now, I need ta ask for a favor.

I came to Gorgrond in search of an expedition of me fellow Dark Irons that were headed this way. Sadly I lost 'em.

I am goin' south to look for them. Thing is, south is nothing but botani, podlings, giant trees, and other mean, angry plants.

Yer lumber camp resources would be mighty appreciated. If ya help me look for me friends I swear we'll help ya in any way we can.

passages.title: Deeproot
passages.text:
Ah good! Ya made it.

The lasses here insisted on comin' with, though they don't seem to like each other much.

passages.title: The Infested
passages.text:
D'kaan did not say it, but there were more rangari taken by the botani than the ones you found.

He believes they were slain. I fear worse.

You might dare to venture into the Razorbloom. If you do, you may discover what the botani do to their... "prisoners."

Give these poor souls a proper release.

passages.title: The Infested
passages.text: One truth of Gorgrond: death is not the worst thing that can happen to you.

passages.title: The Infested
passages.text:
I thank you for doing what I could not.

While it is the right thing to do, it is hard to loose the arrow when your target was once a friend.

passages.title: The Voice of Iyu
passages.text:
Journal Entry 25 -

The botani got themselves a leader who calls himself... er... herself... er... itself the Voice of Iyu.

Seems the botani see the genesaur as gods and only the most bossy of the botani get to speak on behalf of the genesaur.

When we tried askin' it about the artifact we found back at the base it got all angry and sent off Lera and Nori and I ain't seen either of them since.

I got a bad feelin' about this thing.

passages.title: The Voice of Iyu
passages.text:
They mulched my friends? Those pointy branch wavers with their wee beady eyes! Thank ya for avenging ma friends.

We best be findin' the others before they get turned into plant food.

passages.title: Super Seeds
passages.text:
These seeds have been shielded with care by the botani.

Great power can be felt surging out of these tiny vessels of life.

These may prove useful.

passages.title: Super Seeds
passages.text: What have ya found?

passages.title: Super Seeds
passages.text:
I may not know much about farmin' but I do know a power source when I see it. These seeds are packin' quite a punch.

Way to think on yer feet and grab 'em, Commander.

passages.title: Iron Horde Orders
passages.text: Spirit spotted some orders at the Iron Horde camp on the nearby bluff. You must have missed them when you were there. Could you look into it?

passages.title: Iron Horde Orders
passages.text: These orders are written with terrible handwriting.

passages.title: Firing the Mayor
passages.text:
The bottle has a large stopper in it with the label "Property of Mayor Nurg Boltsnap."

As you gaze at the bottle you hear the sound of heavy machinery coming from the nearby marshland. 

An investigation would be prudent. If the mayor has turned he will also need to be put down.

passages.title: A Heavy Helping Hand
passages.text:
Burrian gave us the coordinates of the Dark Iron base. They named it Moira's Reach.

But half way through buildin' it the base got infested with goren.

If you head south you should come to the structure. Just look for a big ol' cannon.

We will follow as soon as we get this bloody tank untangled.

passages.title: A Heavy Helping Hand
passages.text:
Co... Commander? Well ain't you a sight for sore eyes?

I didn't think anyone friendly was comin' for me.

We found an artifact that seemed pretty handy against the locals in the area but then those acid-mouthed roly polies showed up and started eatin' everything.

Help me up an' we can git to it.

passages.title: Old Friends, New Enemies
passages.text:
I cannot believe Orgrim would continue to do Blackhand's bidding after all the destruction he has wrought.

We must confront him. Join me at the village along Orunai Coast and we will confront my oldest friend.

passages.title: Old Friends, New Enemies
passages.text: Orgrim will not stop this foolishness, so we must stop him.

passages.title: Ogre Diplomacy
passages.text:
Ogres are ogres. Spirits or not, the Ango'rosh are not different.

Even with their ritual books, they won't relinquish their power to you until you prove yourself.

I've fought ogres my entire life, and there's only one way to earn that.

Killing them outright.

The more Ango'rosh spirits and their pets as you take out while you're there, the more respect you'll command among them.

passages.title: Ogre Diplomacy
passages.text: I hope you've extended our diplomatic hand to our ogre friends.

passages.title: Ogre Diplomacy
passages.text: Another successful negotiation.

passages.title: Firing the Mayor
passages.text:
Ever since this zombie outbreak began I haven't seen the mayor at all. If he is infected then we could be in for a huge problem if he can escape out of town. Damn, we could be in for another zombie outbreak even!

We got to find him and make sure he doesn't escape! He used to ride in his custom shredder down on the shore line before the fungus started covering up everything. You might find him down there.

passages.title: Spiritual Matters
passages.text:
The spirits of the dead have long been drawn to Oshu'gun.

As long as I can remember, the woods have been filled with ancestral spirits making a ghostly pilgrimage to the heart of the mountain.

However, I fear that what is transpiring here is not the normal spirit walk I have seen before.

Make your way to the Ancestral Grounds and commune with the spirits there for guidance on this matter.

passages.title: Spiritual Matters
passages.text:
The situation here is dire, <name>, but I sensed that we would meet again.

I do not hear the call of the void as loudly as the others, for I am not long dead and my body rests far from this place.

With time though, that will change.

If you are here to help, listen closely for time is short.

passages.title: The Call of Oshu'gun
passages.text:
The elements have spoken and a vision has been revealed, <name>.

Together we shall travel to the great mountain Oshu'gun and put an end to the dark disturbance there.

If what you saw in the vision is to be believed, then great danger awaits us.

I will meet you in the Spirit Woods at the foot of Oshu'gun. When you are ready to depart, speak with Gixmo Moneycash and he will fly you there.

passages.title: The Call of Oshu'gun
passages.text:
It has been many years since I have set foot within these woods.

I was last here for the Kosh'harg many years ago when this place was shared amongst all clans. Those days have past and now only the Warsong banner flies here.

passages.title: Just In Case
passages.text:
When we set up shop the first thing we built was the cannon. Seemed like a good place fer it.

We started buildin' the base up around it when them chompin' acid spittin' varmints came crawlin' out of the ground.

The upside though is the cannon is built, just not loaded.

We have to go down to the bottom floor of this thing anyway so may as well grab some Doomshot if you see any on your way down.

Better to load the cannon and not need it than to need it and not have it loaded.

passages.title: Just In Case
passages.text: Ya got that ammo?

passages.title: Just In Case
passages.text: While I hope we don' need to fire the big gun, I kinda hope we can fire the big gun.

passages.title: Will of the Genesaur
passages.text:
When the goren attacked we threw everything we had at them but they just kept comin'.

So some of the lads went and stole a fancy artifact from the botani.

Problem was we couldn't get it to work. Now the artifact is sitting at the bottom of the bastion. To get to it you got to go all the way to the back of the tunnels past all them goren and find the wee tunnel that takes you farther underground.

If you retrieve it, it is yours.

passages.title: Will of the Genesaur
passages.text: Not fond of this place. If the plants ain't tryin' to kill you then the ground is tryin' to swallow ya up.

passages.title: Will of the Genesaur
passages.text: That artifact was useful until it ran out of juice. Hopefully you got some seeds and water for it.

passages.title: Bled Dry
passages.text:
<The draenei spits out his last words.>

They kept us in cages. They... drain our blood, for... rituals...

<He coughs violently.>

...many left --

 -- my... people...

<The draenei dies.>

passages.title: Bled Dry
passages.text: You should save those draenei, <name>. It is the right thing to do.

passages.title: Bled Dry
passages.text:
Well done, <name>.

Given, they are injured, half-starved, and poorly-equipped... but there is no blade so sharp as a vengeful spirit, no armor so thick as a righteous cause.

passages.title: Vengeance for the Fallen
passages.text:
Too many of my people have fallen at the hands of the Bleeding Hollow. Their cruelty cannot be forgiven.

<The grieving orc looks up at you.>

Make them pay.

passages.title: Vengeance for the Fallen
passages.text: I admire your sense of duty, <name>. Even when your own survival hangs in the balance, you still find time to bring closure to a grieving widow. Well done.

passages.title: Vengeance for the Fallen
passages.text:
Too many of my people have fallen at the hands of the Bleeding Hollow. Their cruelty cannot be forgiven.

<The grieving draenei looks up at you.>

Make them pay.

passages.title: Vengeance for the Fallen
passages.text: I admire your sense of righteousness, <name>. Even when your own survival hangs in the balance, you still find time to avenge a grieving widow. Well done.

passages.title: A Sentimental Relic
passages.text:
My father's bangle sat here for ages before that imposter Ikiss stole it away.

I thank you for returning it, but I have no need for keepsakes. Take it, with my blessing.

If there are still Talonpriests loyal to the true Talon King, please bring it to them.

passages.title: A Sentimental Relic
passages.text: Hm? What's that you have there?

passages.title: A Sentimental Relic
passages.text:
Lithic actually spoke to you? Or, some shade of her at least... 

Fascinating!

passages.title: Zero Xuks Given
passages.text:
The spirits have spoken to me. They believe the magnaron, Gro the Uncreator, will join our fight and lead his underlings against the Iron Horde.

This is an honor beyond any bestowed upon a Laughing Skull, at least in my time.

I will commune with the magnaron, and together we shall destroy the Iron Horde.

passages.title: Zero Xuks Given
passages.text: The spirits of my ancestors have betrayed me! Their skulls are surely laughing.

passages.title: Powering the Defenses
passages.text:
It's good to see a Horde champion joining the fight.

Auchindoun's defenses are faltering quickly. The few Auchenai soulpriests not on the front are working fervently to maintain them.

Soulbinder Tuulani went inside the nearby Tomb of Lights to retrieve a backup power pylon and hasn't returned. If you can find her and get her and the pylon back here safely it would help greatly.

passages.title: Powering the Defenses
passages.text: You look like you can fight. We need to get out of here!

passages.title: Test Quest
The Bounty of Bladespire
passages.text:
The sacking of this fortress is as much your victory as ours. It is only fair you should share in the bounty.

I had the men prepare a chest for you. Take what you will.

passages.title: The Bounty of Bladespire
passages.text: This camp of yours could be fruitful, but it rests upon the footstep of Grom'gar. The Thunderlords are not likely to be welcome neighbors.

passages.title: Retribution for the Light
passages.text:
There are agents of darkness everywhere, fighting tooth and nail to envelop the world. The Light relies on us to balance the scale.

You have the power needed to destroy Teron'gor's demonic minions once and for all. Send them to the Twisting Nether in pieces!

passages.title: Retribution for the Light
passages.text: Already I can feel the Light triumphing over darkness. We've done it!

passages.title: Power of the Genesaur
passages.text:
Commander, you now have the Will of the Genesaur along with the genesis water and enough seeds to grow an army. Not to mention the lives of the dwarves you saved.

I would call this mission a success.

I can help the dwarves mop up their operation here and see what we can salvage. In the meantime, you may want to bring the artifact to Maraad back at the outpost.

passages.title: Power of the Genesaur
passages.text:
Well done, Commander. Many of the orcs have tried to master the power of the genesaur but I have never heard of any of them reaching this level of success.

This should provide us a substantial advantage in the days ahead.

passages.title: A Heart Unbroken
passages.text:
Though Gordawg's body lays shattered and lifeless upon the ground, a crystal heart glows brightly. The large crystal appears to be fully intact and all that remains of the mighty earthen fury.

Perhaps Kalandrios will know what to make of the crystal.

passages.title: Power Unearthed
passages.text:
What power could reduce a village to ashes in the blink of an eye? The Adherents claim it is the will of Rukhmar.

A lie, obviously.

They did nothing to earn such power - in truth, they stumbled upon it rather unwittingly, in a hole in the ground.

Come and visit me near the excavation site just west of here. We must understand their technology if we are to defeat it.

passages.title: Power Unearthed
passages.text: Ah yes, you've arrived just in time.

passages.title: Legacy of the Apexis
passages.text:
The Apexis are long gone, but their legacy lies preserved in ancient chambers beneath Arak.

Legions of dormant constructs; crystals flush with solar energy; magical techniques lost to the ages - the Apexis left behind caches of immense power, which the Adherents of Rukhmar have begun to unearth.

Bring me the cores of the re-activated constructs patrolling the excavation site. Those crystals are the basis of Apexis technology, and the key to our enemy's devastating power.

passages.title: Legacy of the Apexis
passages.text: The Apexis had every advantage, and yet they vanished. What could have happened?

passages.title: Legacy of the Apexis
passages.text: Excellent. With these we can begin to understand.

passages.title: Sol Sisters
passages.text:
When I was still a guard in Skyreach, I was tasked with protecting the sisters Veoryx and Krashyx.

They were prodigies. At an age when most sun acolytes could barely read, the sisters conjured familiars of pure sunlight to illuminate their textbooks in the small hours.

Now they unravel the secrets of Apexis technology, and their excavation has just breached two ancient chambers.

Enter those chambers and cut down the sisters before they reap the terrible rewards of their discovery.

passages.title: Sol Sisters
passages.text: <The Sol-Shapers are using their power to awaken these ancient Apexis constructs.>

passages.title: Sol Sisters
passages.text: <The core of this slumbering construct begins to hum softly.>

passages.title: Shot-Caller
passages.text:
<Solar energy courses through the slumbering constructs, their ancient servos whirring to life all around you. It is too late to shut them down now.

Outside, an arakkoa overseer bellows commands, each answered by the buzz of an Apexis beam carving away at the mountain.

That turret would make short work of the constructs - if you can command it.>

passages.title: Shot-Caller
passages.text: <A comfortable-looking chair with a socket in the arm rest.>

passages.title: Shot-Caller
passages.text:
<The Apexis interface slides into place with a satisfying click. Seems this is the seat for taking full command of the turret.

Rifling through the cushions, you find a few spare coins, which you pocket.>

passages.title: The Warsong Threat
passages.text:
<The attack plans are scrawled onto the parchment in thick, black ink and bound in rough leather.>

To all outrider stations:

The warlord has commanded that all outriders prepare for a full assault upon the Horde invaders in our land. Plans for the attack have been delivered to several of the remote outrider posts.

Blood and glory shall be ours as we trample the Horde invaders beneath our feet!

The warlord commands and the Warsong obey! Lok'tar ogar!

passages.title: The Warsong Threat
passages.text: What do you have for me?

passages.title: The Warsong Threat
passages.text:
<Blood Guard Ehanes looks over the attack plans.>

Hmm... I see. You have done well to retrieve these attack plans. With the plans in our hands, we will be more than prepared to counter the assault when it comes.

passages.title: One of Our Own
passages.text:
Da bird-men captured me while I was gettin' da lay a da land.

We been workin' on an outpost for you just round dis mountain so your will be spreadin' all over da continent.

Things not be goin' well.

I be needin' your assistance, commander. Can you tell dem that I mean no harm so I can be showin' you da outpost?

passages.title: One of Our Own
passages.text: You be savin' my hide, commander.

passages.title: One of Our Own
passages.text: Thank da spirits you showed up. Dey hear my prayers.

passages.title: One of Our Own
passages.text:
These wretched creatures captured me while I was scouting the area. Now that you're here, commander, we could really use your help back at base.

Oh, and any way you could convince your... friends... to let me go?

They, uh... won't let me leave.

passages.title: One of Our Own
passages.text: I had really hoped to have given you a better impression when you came out here.

passages.title: One of Our Own
passages.text:
Now, uh... could we maybe forget this little incident happened, commander?

Bodrick and the other agents would never let me live this down.

passages.title: Inspecting the Troops
passages.text:
Axefall be just a moment's ride from here.

I be markin' da location on your map and meet you dere.

passages.title: Inspecting the Troops
passages.text: Our lives for your will, commander.

passages.title: Inspecting the Troops
passages.text:
Southport lies not far from here to the southwest.

No time for chit-chat. I will meet you there, commander.

passages.title: Inspecting the Troops
passages.text: I hope everything is to your liking. It's been one hell of a job.

passages.title: Orders, Commander?
passages.text:
Commander, our status report is... regrettable.

We'll be out of supplies in a few days' time, and that's assuming we have any troops left by then. 

There's just enough material left to put up an inn or a trading post.

The inn would allow us to station fresh troops here, but the trading post would open up potential supply routes with the outcasts nearby.

I've left out Gazlowe's blueprints on the drafting table. We await your will.

passages.title: Orders, Commander?
passages.text:
Have you made a choice, commander?

Give the word and it will be done.

passages.title: Orders, Commander?
passages.text:
Your will be done.

For the Horde!

passages.title: Follow that Hotrod!
passages.text:
Miss Kimzee is one tough nugget but Pinchwhistle Point is too dangerous for her to handle alone. It'll be a catastrophe for morale if our boss gets infected.

I need to get these crewmen back to the Gearworks so I need you to go and make sure she is alright.

Her uncle's place is the tower just on the other side of the oil fields; I think you should look for her around there.

passages.title: Follow that Hotrod!
passages.text:
I have good news and bad news.

The good news is my uncle's alive! The bad news is his leg is injured and we're surrounded by infected! With my hotrod wrecked we can't get him out of here.

passages.title: Orders, Commander?
passages.text:
Commander <name>, it's an honor.

We're barely holding on, <sir/madame>. We have a week's supplies at best, assuming we have any troops left to supply in that time.

We have just enough material left to put up an inn or a trading post.

The inn would allow us to station reinforcements here, while the trading post would allow supply routes with the outcasts nearby.

We need your authorization for the project, commander. It's your decision.

passages.title: Orders, Commander?
passages.text: Glory to your forces, commander.

passages.title: Orders, Commander?
passages.text: Praise the Light you're here. I thought we were going to have to wait until a courier could reach you for a decision on this.

passages.title: Old Friends
passages.text:
Admiral Taylor was ordered to establish a garrison inland while we erected yours in Shadowmoon Valley. He settled just a short ways north of here.

The two of us could go there and borrow some supplies to tide us over before our next shipment.

What do you say, commander? I'm sure the admiral will be thrilled to see you again.

passages.title: Old Friends
passages.text: What in the king's name happened here?

passages.title: What's Theirs is Ours
passages.text:
I found somethin' else while I was scoutin', boss.

Da Alliance have a garrison just across da way, and der been no movement in or out of da place in a good while.

Dis be a golden opportunity to sack da place and bolster your coffers, commander.

What do ya say? We do it together.

passages.title: What's Theirs is Ours
passages.text: Everyone be dead, mon. What did dis?

passages.title: Tainted Garden
passages.text:
The abandonded mine shaft has been overrun with Goren! They seem to be responding to commands from a big one further down in the mine. If you can take him out, the rest will probably retreat.

Once you have those Goren cleared out, we can get that mine up and working!

passages.title: Flame On
passages.text:
Alright <name>, we've saved as many as we could but now we need to make sure this disaster doesn't spread any further.

The firebombs are wired up and ready to go.

Kimzee just finished work on the flying machine so we're ready to ride back to the Gearworks as soon as we're finished.

You've done all the hard work so I think you should get the honors of triggering it.

passages.title: Flame On
passages.text:
<name>, you did fantastic work.

Everyone here at the Gearworks owes you big time for what you've done for us.

Here, I want to give you little something. Think of it as a personal token of my gratitude.

passages.title: I See Dead People
passages.text:
Everybody here be... dead.

Dis architect's spirit not be wantin' to fight us. Even in death he only be wantin' to work. Maybe we can break da haze over him and get to da bottom of dis.

I bet one of da spectral laborers be havin' one of his schematics we can show to him to clear his mind.

passages.title: I See Dead People
passages.text: I'd recognize one of my schematics anywhere.

passages.title: I See Dead People
passages.text: Thank you, friend.

passages.title: I See Dead People
passages.text:
Th... they're ghosts! All of them!

Bryan was one of my best friends. Something is clouding his mind; we need to snap him out of it and get to the bottom of this!

He was always obsessed with his work. Maybe showing him one of his schematics would help. One of the spectral laborers might have one.

passages.title: I See Dead People
passages.text: I'd recognize one of my schematics anywhere.

passages.title: I See Dead People
passages.text: Thank you, friend.

passages.title: Called to the Throne
passages.text:
I was far from here in Talador when the voice called out to me.

I looked around but found myself alone. Again, I heard the voice as if it were a breeze in my mind.

"You are needed at the throne," it whispered.

The voice called itself Kalandrios, and it guided me to this place.

I had never been here before, nor had I yet beheld these furies with my eyes; yet this feels strangely familiar to me as if it happened long ago in a forgotten dream.

We should greet the furies and hear them out.

passages.title: Called to the Throne
passages.text: Are you ready to commune with the elemental spirits of the throne?

passages.title: Called to the Throne
passages.text:
I am not sure what to make of this.

The elements are no longer in balance? The great fury Gordawg is missing and must be found?

The furies appear noble, and deep within my soul their words ring true.

I believe we aid should them in their cause.

passages.title: Nobundo Sends Word
passages.text:
Your presence has been requested at the Throne of Elements, <name>.

Vindicator Nobundo has heard the call of the furies upon the wind and made the journey to commune with the elements.

I know not what the intentions of the furies are, but they are revered as noble and powerful spirits by the orcs.

passages.title: Nobundo Sends Word
passages.text:
I am glad to see that you have arrived safely.

Come, there is much work to be done here.

passages.title: Elemental Attunement
passages.text:
Even now, as we speak, the voice of Kalandrios continues to whisper to my mind.

"The Hero of Azeroth must attune to the elements of the plateau."

Upon the Elemental Plateau are four great pillars carved of living rock. Lay your hands upon the stone pillars and your soul will be attuned with the elements.

I will continue to commune with the great furies and attempt to further understand their will while you journey to the plateau.

passages.title: Elemental Attunement
passages.text:
I see a fire within your eyes and a wind upon your step, <name>.

If what Kalandrios speaks is true, you have attuned your life energy with each of the elemental forces on Draenor.

The voice says that you are now ready to undertake the Ritual of Binding.

Return to me when your work upon the plateau is finished and we will speak further.

passages.title: Shooting the Breeze
passages.text:
Kia and I are having a spirited debate over who kills more efficiently: SI:7 or rangari.

Care to get in on the wager, commander?

I've been focusing on talbuk because of their fierce majesty. They truly encapsulate the grandeur of Nagrand as any native of Draenor knows.

passages.title: Shooting the Breeze
passages.text:
This outsider really thinks she can come here and best me in my own land?

Oh... sorry, commander. Present company excluded, of course.

passages.title: Shooting the Breeze
passages.text:
Twenty-four, huh? That's fine work.

I brought back fifty.

I'll send someone out for the meat. Waste not, want not.

passages.title: What Happened Here?
passages.text:
Dis architect's spirit not be wantin' to fight us. Maybe we can break da haze over his mind and find out what happened.

I bet one of da undead peasants has one of his schematics or somethin' we can show to him to clear his mind.

It be worth a shot.

passages.title: Defection of Gronnstalker Rokash
passages.text:
You have done me a great service. This blade is as much yours as it is mine.

I offer you this blood oath: I shall serve your cause and lend my knowledge of blades and mining to your forces.

Will you accept it?

passages.title: Defection of Gronnstalker Rokash
passages.text: You have proven yourself more powerful than my previous leaders. My service is yours.

passages.title: The Mysterious Flask
passages.text:
The liquid swirling around inside the flask clearly has strong alchemical properties, but its nature is beyond your training.

You have heard that one of the Eventide villagers at your garrison has some knowledge of the alchemy of Draenor. Perhaps he could tell you more?

passages.title: The Mysterious Flask
passages.text: Ah. I see you have found a creation of Draenor alchemy.

passages.title: The Young Alchemist
passages.text:
I learned a little about alchemy from my aunt. If you want to know more, though, you should speak with my cousin Abatha. She was apprenticing under my aunt before she passed away.

Abatha lives near the Verdant Mire with her father and sister.

passages.title: The Young Alchemist
passages.text: Please. Help me. I need to find my father.

passages.title: The Missing Father
passages.text:
I would be happy to help with your alchemical inquiries, but right now I am worried about my father.

It's been quite some time since he went hunting down by the river, but he still hasn't returned home. I need to watch Lumiel. Will you please find him?

passages.title: The Missing Father
passages.text: Thank you, stranger. I don't think the razorfangs were happy that I was hunting the same prey.

passages.title: Queen of the Clefthoof
passages.text:
Laara told me that they have Banthar here! Or rather, that she's still alive back now. Did what I just said make any sense?

This is our chance, commander. We can defeat a younger, more powerful version of Banthar and really stick it to these rangari.

We'll show Laara how a true professional works.

passages.title: Queen of the Clefthoof
passages.text: Banthar's horn. Hemet would be green with envy to have another shot at such a powerful beast.

passages.title: Queen of the Clefthoof
passages.text: Magnificent kill, commander. You've done us all proud.

passages.title: Someone's Missing Arrow
passages.text: <An arrow of rangari make is sticking out of the side of this talbuk. Perhaps Rangari Laara will be interested in your find.>

passages.title: Someone's Missing Arrow
passages.text: That's MY arrow! Where'd you get it?

passages.title: The Call of Oshu'gun
passages.text:
The elements have spoken and a vision has been revealed, <name>.

Together we shall travel to the great mountain Oshu'gun and put an end to the dark disturbance there.

If what you saw in the vision is to be believed, then great danger awaits us.

I will meet you in the Spirit Woods at the foot of Oshu'gun. When you are ready to depart, speak with Gixmo Moneycash and he will fly you to there.

passages.title: The Call of Oshu'gun
passages.text:
These woods are sacred to the orcs and to my people as well.

Beneath the great mountain of Oshu'gun lies the heart of Nagrand, the Genedar. This great dimensional vessel rescued my people from annihilation and brought us to this world.

passages.title: Queen of the Clefthoof
passages.text:
Ogka told me that they have Banthar here! Or rather, that she's still alive back now. Did what I just said make any sense?

This is our chance, commander. We can defeat a younger, more powerful version of Banthar and really stick it to these frostwolves.

We'll show Ogka how a true professional works.

passages.title: Queen of the Clefthoof
passages.text: Banthar's horn. Hemet would be green with envy to have another shot at such a powerful beast.

passages.title: Queen of the Clefthoof
passages.text: Magnificent kill, commander. You've done us all proud.

passages.title: Shooting the Breeze
passages.text:
Taz and I are having a spirited debate over who kills more efficiently: shadow hunters or frostwolves.

Care to get in on the wager, commander?

I've been focusing on talbuk because of their fierce majesty. They truly encapsulate the grandeur of Nagrand as any native of Draenor knows.

passages.title: Shooting the Breeze
passages.text:
This outsider really thinks he can come here and best me in my own land?

Oh... sorry, commander. Present company excluded, of course.

passages.title: Shooting the Breeze
passages.text:
Twenty-four, huh? That's fine work.

I brought back fifty.

I'll send someone out for the meat. Waste not, want not.

passages.title: Someone's Missing Axe
passages.text: <A throwing axe of frostwolf make is sticking out of the side of this talbuk. Perhaps Stalker Ogka will be interested in your find.>

passages.title: Someone's Missing Axe
passages.text: That's MY axe! Where'd you get it?

passages.title: Second in Command
passages.text:
Wait... I remember something else.

Sir Edward... he was shouting... looking for someone.

I... I can't remember who. There were so many screams...

passages.title: Second in Command
passages.text: If today was any other day I'd have you court-martialed for being out of uniform.

passages.title: The Warsong Threat
passages.text:
<The attack plans are scrawled onto the parchment in thick, black ink and bound in rough leather.>

To all outrider stations:

The warlord has commanded that all outriders prepare for a full assault upon the Alliance invaders in our land. Plans for the attack have been delivered to several of the remote outrider posts.

Blood and glory shall be ours as we trample the Alliance invaders beneath our feet!

The warlord commands and the Warsong obey! Lok'tar ogar!

passages.title: The Warsong Threat
passages.text: What do you have for me?

passages.title: The Warsong Threat
passages.text:
<Captain Washburn examines the attack plans, squinting at the lettering and holding the pages upside down.>

Hmm... I see... yes... indeed!

These are obviously attack plans, as you yourself have stated, but they are most likely written by kobold pyromancers.

Strange though, I haven't seen any kobold pyromancers since my days in Azeroth. No matter! I assure you that the outpost is well armed and mostly fireproof!

If we are attacked, the outpost shan't fall. You have my word, commander!

passages.title: Through The Nether
passages.text:
The void rituals have been disrupted, but dark energy still flows into the nether beacons at the ritual sites. This can only mean that the beacons are being powered from within the Twisting Nether itself.

The only way to sever the flow of void energy to the beacons is to travel into the Twisting Nether and stop whatever power lurks there!

Use a beacon to travel to the Twisting Nether. Once there, us the shaman stone given to us by the furies to contact me.

Light be with you.

passages.title: The Void March
passages.text:
Legions of void terrors are marching upon Oshu'gun and sacrificing themselves to the void lord Invalidus.

As they die Invalidus grows stronger. It is as if the lesser creatures only serve to feed the void lord.

We must stop Invalidus from becoming so powerful that it cannot be stopped.

Slay as many void monsters as you can, to slow the growth of Invalidus. In the meantime, I will search for a way to encounter Invalidus before it is too late to stop it.

passages.title: Silence The Call
passages.text:
The Warsong shaman are using the elements to channel dark energy from the void.

I am no shaman, but even I know that such practices are abhored by most orc clans. The power of the void is opposite to the Light, and a source of entropy and destruction.

These rituals thin the veil between our world and the Twisting Nether. Should the rituals continue, this land will soon be overrun by the denizens of the Twisting Nether.

Slay the shaman leading these dark rituals before destruction falls upon us!

passages.title: The Shadow Over Oshu'gun
passages.text:
The void lord Invalidus stands atop the peak of Oshu'gun gorging itself upon the souls of the dead.

Even the fallen void terrors that you slew only served to feed the monster.

If we do not act now, Invalidus will grow too powerful to encounter alone.

At each of the ritual sites in the Twisting Nether, there is a crystal filled with the powers of the void. Disturb the void crystal and Invalidus will sense your presence.

Be ready, Invalidus will waste no time in attempting to feed on your soul.

passages.title: Disrupt The Rituals
passages.text:
Beneath the mountain of Oshu'gun the Warsong perform dark rituals.

The Warsong shaman seek to empower their clan by drawing upon a great source of void energy within the heart of Oshu'gun.

Though I do not know for certain the source of this power...I fear that the dying naaru K'ure may be involved.

The Warsong rituals must be stopped or the veil that separates this world from the Twisting Nether will be ripped apart.

Locate the ritual totems used to channel these rituals and destroy them.

passages.title: The Nether Approaches
passages.text:
By drawing upon the power of the void, the Warsong have thinned the veil that shields our world from the Twisting Nether.

Portals are opening within the nether that threaten to connect the terrors of the void to Draenor.

Should these portals fully open, the path will be clear for all manner of demons and void creatures to rampage across Nagrand.

Go and collapse the portals before they become functional!

passages.title: Spiritual Matters
passages.text:
The spirits of the dead have long been drawn to the mountain of Oshu'gun.

As long as I can remember, the woods have been filled with ancestral spirits making a ghostly pilgrimage to the heart of the mountain. I fear that the souls drawn to Oshu'gun are being consumed by the growing void within the mountain.

Make your way to the Ancestral Grounds and commune with the spirits there for guidance.

passages.title: Spiritual Matters
passages.text:
The situation here is dire, <name>, but I sensed that we would meet again.

I do not hear the call of the void as loudly as the others, for I am not long dead and my body rests far from this place.

With time though, that will change.

If you are here to help, listen closely for time is short.

passages.title: The Pale Threat
passages.text:
In the time that you have been fighting against the void, I have been exploring the disturbance within Shadowfall Canyon.

A dark mist has settled in the canyon, <name>; and I found twisted, pale creatures lurking there.

We have much to discuss. Return to me from the Twisting Nether and we will speak more.

passages.title: The Fate of Gordawg
passages.text:
Looming monstrously between us and the inner chamber is the great fury we have sought to return to the Throne of Elements.

Gordawg stands before us enthralled; a slave to Cho'gall. My heart is heavy with grief to see such a great creature mindless and enslaved by evil.

There is no going back, in order to push forward you must go through Gordawg.

It pains me, but Gordawg must be slain.

Slay Gordawg and return the fury's heart to the Throne of Elements where it belongs.

passages.title: The Fate of Gordawg
passages.text: What of Gordawg? Has the great fury been brought to rest?

passages.title: The Fate of Gordawg
passages.text:
Gordawg was a mighty ally. The elements will mourn the loss of the fury, but death was the only answer. Gordawg would not have wished to stay a slave to evil.

Though Gordawg is no more, the heart of a fury is eternal and unbreakable. In time, this brightly glowing heart will take shape into a new earthen fury.

Such is the cycle of life upon the Elemental Plateau.

passages.title: The Pale Threat
passages.text:
If we are to succeed in stopping Cho'gall from destroying the naaru, we will need to fight our way through the Underpale; a dark, winding cavern infested with the Pale.

The Pale are fallen orcs that despise all that is good and holy. The longer they are left to their devices beneath the ground, the further their dark plots progress.

Make your way into the Underpale, slay the vile creatures within and take out their leader, Greyseer.

passages.title: The Pale Threat
passages.text:
The Pale are wretched creatures that hate the Light and plot against the innocent. Without Greyseer to lead them, they will be disorganized and in chaos for a time.

Should a new leader arise from within their ranks, we shall smite them down once more.

passages.title: Dark Binding
passages.text:
Even as we speak, the pale are enslaving an army of elementals in Shadowfall Canyon. Many have already been enslaved and if we do not lend our aid, more will follow.

Go to Shadowfall Canyon and set free the elemental spirits which are not yet fully enthralled by the pale. As for those already enslaved, the only mercy we can give them now is a swift death.

passages.title: Dark Binding
passages.text: You have done well to free the elemental spirits from their bonds. If Cho'gall and the pale seek an army of elemental slaves, they must not be allowed to succeed.

passages.title: The Infested
passages.text:
I understand Kaz's desire to rescue her people, but her plan is reckless and she is not telling us everything.

I came along to make sure she wasn't devising a plan against us and now I see this... this... horror.

What did the botani do to these orcs?

These infested souls need to be put to rest. Give them peace.

passages.title: The Infested
passages.text:
These creatures... were not what I expected to see. I always knew Gorgrond to be a dangerous place, but I never could have guessed at how vile.

Thank you, commander, for your compassion in this.

passages.title: The Voice of Iyu
passages.text:
The botani and their wretched minions take and take and take.

They want food, they take our land. They want an army, they take our people.

It is important to strike fear into the shrubby hearts of these plant people.

Look for their leader, the Voice of Iyu. It is a botani who speaks on behalf of their genesaur master.

Kill their precious leader in the safety of his precious bloom.

passages.title: The Voice of Iyu
passages.text:
It isn't enough to kill the botani. They will always have greater numbers.

You must cut them deep and hard, where it hurts them the most.

Like slaying their most sacred leader.

passages.title: Super Seeds
passages.text:
These seeds have been shielded with care by the botani.

Great power can be felt surging out of these tiny vessels of life.

These may prove useful.

passages.title: Super Seeds
passages.text: What have you found?

passages.title: Super Seeds
passages.text:
Seeds. So simple to look at but in each the potential for untold amounts of destruction. Much like my son.

You were wise to take these.

passages.title: Punishable by Death
passages.text:
Traitors, the lot!

You're looking at the last bastion of forces still loyal to Admiral Taylor and the Alliance.

I'll be damned if the defectors get away clean.

You look like you're ready. Show them how we deal with their kind during times of war.

passages.title: Punishable by Death
passages.text: Well fought. For the Alliance!

passages.title: Prime the Cannons
passages.text:
The armory is lost to the traitors. All we have left are these few cannons with no ammunition.

Soldier, I need you to recover cannonballs so we can get these things running.

Actually, one more cannon wouldn't hurt, either.

passages.title: Prime the Cannons
passages.text: I hope you're toting a cannon and some balls, soldier.

passages.title: Prime the Cannons
passages.text: Good job, soldier.

passages.title: Power of the Genesaur
passages.text:
Commander, you now have the Will of the Genesaur along with the genesis water and enough seeds to grow an army. Not to mention the Laughing Skulls you helped save.

I would call this mission a success.

I will investigate this fortress further and see if there are more materials we might glean from it.

In the meantime, you may want to bring these artifacts you have obtained to Durotan back at the outpost. I will catch up once we have finished here.

passages.title: Power of the Genesaur
passages.text:
Well done, Commander. Many of the orcs have tried to master the power of the genesaur but I have never heard of any succeeding.

You have won us a powerful weapon for the next time we face the Iron Horde.

passages.title: Pollen Power
passages.text:
Those of us who grew up in Gorgrond have long learned a few secrets of the botani that can be used to grow our own plants.

There is no such thing as a hungry Laughing Skull for this reason.

The ravagers are the key.

Outside of Evermorn Springs you will find ravagers of every type. Slay them and bring me the pollen they carry, and I can cultivate it to be of use to your garrison.

passages.title: Pollen Power
passages.text: Few dare challenge the botani in the field of growing plants.

passages.title: Pollen Power
passages.text: Ah... yes, yes, yes. Fresh pollen. With a dash of a few secret ingredients you can feed an army with the food you could grow from this, if you know the secret ways.

passages.title: Cutter
passages.text:
You found many Laughing Skulls. All friends, all loved, all dead. But you did not find my precious Cutter.

They must have taken him to Evermorn Springs.

Find him, and rescue him.

He is a good boy, and deserves a better death than infesting.

I am going to round up some ravagers and take the place by air. Look for me in Evermorn if you find Cutter before I do.

passages.title: Cutter
passages.text:
The botani took my dad. They took my friends. And now they are making me eat fruit!

Why are they so mean?!

Did you kill them all?

I think you should kill them.

passages.title: The Best Poison
passages.text:
Do you like poisons? I am more of a "set everything on fire and loot what doesn't burn" kind of orc myself.

But I do know a thing or two about poisons.

When you venture into the Razor Bloom, look for a pungent, violent plant that we call Reaver Vine. Under just the right circumstances, and FIRE, the vine will make a lovely poison. Bring me some and I shall concoct a lovely poison for you.

passages.title: Cut Them Down
passages.text:
They steal children? Children?!

Had you not rescued Kaz's child, he would be reduced to mulch just like the others.

You should send them a message they will understand. Cut down their great dew casters. Rip them apart.

Let them know that it is not okay to take our children.

passages.title: Cut Them Down
passages.text: They are lucky you are the one that killed them. I would have tried to carve pictures in their dead wood bodies.

passages.title: The Southern Wilds
passages.text:
First the Iron Horde, then the Shadowmoon orcs, and now there's trouble brewing to the south!

My brother is a feyrider to the south, at the Draakorium.

He says that creatures from the swamp are venturing onto our lands. What is this world coming to?

Anyway, you look like a seasoned adventurer. If you are heading that way, would you mind checking in over there?

passages.title: The Southern Wilds
passages.text: Thank you for coming to our aid.

passages.title: The Southern Wilds
passages.text:
I've heard disturbing news from our friends at The Draakorium, to the south.

The town lies near a swamp, and recently, dangerous creatures have been venturing near its borders.

You seem like a seasoned adventurer. If you are heading that way, would you mind checking in with our people there?

I would feel much better if I knew they were safe.

passages.title: The Southern Wilds
passages.text: Ah, Prelate Luari sent you, did she? Such a sweet woman, always looking out for others.

passages.title: The Southern Wilds
passages.text:
Posted by: Prelate Reenu

Noble friends of the Alliance, the draenei of The Draakorium greet you peacefully.

The Draakorium is being attacked by enemies from the nearby swamps.

An Azerothian caravan passed through recently, and may have ventured into dangerous territory.

Any capable adventurer who can assist us with this problem will be rewarded handsomely.

passages.title: The Southern Wilds
passages.text: Thank you for coming to assist us.

passages.title: Under Siege
passages.text:
Those Iron Horde cannons are laying waste to our troops. I'm not sure how much more of this we can handle. Our forces are already spread too thin.

There has to be a way to stop those war machines.

passages.title: Under Siege
passages.text: It will take the Iron Horde quite a while to get those demolishers operational again. Excellent work, <name>.

passages.title: Subversive Scouts
passages.text:
We have been unable to execute a vast majority of our battleplans. We are definitely being watched.

The Iron Horde must have scouts planted throughout the Blasted Lands. Victory is slipping away from us.

passages.title: Subversive Scouts
passages.text: You killed how many scouts? No wonder we have been unable to execute our plans...

passages.title: Ending Executions
passages.text:
We arrived as soon as we could... but we are too late. Nethergarde has fallen. The Iron Horde has taken a number of Nethergarde warriors prisoner.

No doubt they are trying to squeeze vital information out of our troops.

I fear once they are done with their interrogation they will not hesitate to execute their prisoners. Time is running out.

passages.title: Ending Executions
passages.text: Did you kill the Ironmarch Executioners?

passages.title: Ending Executions
passages.text: The prisoners are shaken up, but they are free. Their families are in your debt, <name>.

passages.title: We Burn the Dead
passages.text:
I saw lots of bodies here. Kaz always said to burn the bodies.

That way they can't come back as the mean greens.

We should burn the bodies.

passages.title: We Burn the Dead
passages.text: Hee hee.

passages.title: We Burn the Dead
passages.text: That was stinky.

passages.title: Death to the Dreadmaul
passages.text:
The stupidity of the Dreadmaul ogres never ceases to amaze me. The Iron Horde is clearly using them to further their own nefarious agenda.

Regardless, we must show the ogres what happens when you confront the Alliance. I think it's time we send the Dreadmaul ogres a message.

passages.title: Death to the Dreadmaul
passages.text: It's important that our enemies understand what happens when you attack the Alliance. I'm glad you could be there to show them.

passages.title: For Nethergarde!
passages.text:
The Iron Horde controls Nethergarde Keep, but they are fools if they think we will not return to claim our land.

My best troops are more than eager to spill the blood of those savages, but we need a champion like yourself to lead the charge.

passages.title: For Nethergarde!
passages.text: The Iron Horde will learn to fear us, as they should.

passages.title: Mementos of the Fallen
passages.text:
